questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (property) with List-II (observation):
List-I
(a) Malleability
(b) Ductility
(c) Sonority
(d) Metallic lustre
List-II
(i) A metal strip rings when dropped on the floor
(ii) A metal surface shines after rubbing with sand paper
(iii) A metal flattens into a thin sheet on hammering
(iv) A metal is drawn into a thin wire
questions.explanation:
(a) Malleability means being beaten into sheets, so (a)-(iii).
(b) Ductility means being drawn into wires, so (b)-(iv).
(c) Sonority means producing a ringing sound, so (c)-(i).
(d) Metallic lustre means a shining surface, so (d)-(ii).
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: The term 'anode mud' in electrolytic refining refers to:
options: Soluble impurities that dissolve in the electrolyte
Pure metal deposited on the cathode
Gas bubbles formed at the anode
Insoluble impurities that settle at the bottom below the anode
questions.explanation:
When current passes, metal from the anode dissolves into the electrolyte.
Soluble impurities also go into the solution.
Insoluble impurities cannot dissolve, so they settle at the bottom below the anode. This deposit is called anode mud.
Option (1) is tempting, but soluble impurities stay in the solution and are not anode mud.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following metals react with steam but NOT with cold or hot water?
Aluminium, Iron, Calcium, Zinc, Magnesium, Lead, Copper
questions.explanation:
Aluminium, iron and zinc react only with steam. That makes 3.
Calcium reacts with cold water.
Magnesium reacts with hot water.
Lead and copper do not react even with steam.
So the count is 3.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The hydrogen gas evolved when calcium reacts with cold water does not catch fire.
Reason (R): Calcium starts floating during its reaction with water because bubbles of hydrogen stick to its surface.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation:
A is true. The reaction of calcium with water is less violent than that of sodium or potassium. The heat evolved is not enough to ignite the hydrogen.
R is true. Hydrogen bubbles stick to the calcium and make it float.
R explains why calcium floats. It does not explain why the hydrogen fails to catch fire, which depends on how much heat is released.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (metal) with List-II (method suitable for obtaining it), keeping the activity series in mind:
List-I
(a) Potassium
(b) Zinc
(c) Mercury
(d) Manganese
List-II
(i) Heating its sulphide ore in air alone
(ii) Electrolysis of its molten compound
(iii) Roasting or calcination followed by reduction with carbon
(iv) Heating its oxide with aluminium powder
questions.explanation:
(a) Potassium is at the top of the activity series. Carbon cannot reduce its oxide, so it needs electrolytic reduction: (ii).
(b) Zinc is of medium reactivity. ZnS is roasted or $ZnCO_3$ is calcined to ZnO, which carbon then reduces: (iii).
(c) Mercury is of low reactivity. Heating HgS in air gives HgO, which further heating reduces to Hg: (i).
(d) Manganese is obtained by the displacement reaction $3MnO_2 + 4Al \rightarrow 3Mn + 2Al_2O_3$: (iv).
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which of the following arrangements shows the metals in the correct order of DECREASING reactivity?
options: Zn > Al > Mg > Fe
Fe > Zn > Al > Mg
Al > Mg > Fe > Zn
Mg > Al > Zn > Fe
questions.explanation:
The activity series places these metals in the order Mg, then Al, then Zn, then Fe, from most to least reactive.
The same order appears in the reaction with dilute HCl. Magnesium gives bubbles fastest and the most heat.
Option (2) is this order reversed.
Option (3) wrongly places Al above Mg.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Three metals P, Q and R were added separately to three salt solutions. The results are given below ('Yes' = displacement occurred, 'No' = no reaction).
Metal | ZnSO4 | FeSO4 | CuSO4
P | No | Yes | Yes
Q | No | No | Yes
R | Yes | Yes | Yes
What is the correct order of decreasing reactivity?
options: R > P > Q
P > R > Q
Q > P > R
R > Q > P
questions.explanation:
R displaces Zn, Fe and Cu, so R is above zinc and is the most reactive.
P displaces Fe and Cu but not Zn, so P lies between zinc and iron.
Q displaces only Cu, so Q lies between iron and copper.
The order is therefore R > P > Q.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Sodium metal is obtained by passing electric current through molten sodium chloride. Which of the following statements about this process is correct?
options: Chlorine gas is liberated at the cathode by the reaction $2Cl^- \rightarrow Cl_2 + 2e^-$
Sodium is deposited at the cathode, which is the negatively charged electrode, by the reaction $Na^+ + e^- \rightarrow Na$
Sodium is deposited at the anode because $Na^+$ ions lose electrons there
Sodium chloride is used as an aqueous solution so that the ions can move freely
questions.explanation:
During electrolysis of molten NaCl, the Na$^+$ ions move to the cathode (negative electrode). There each ion gains an electron: Na$^+$ + e$^-$ → Na.
The Cl$^-$ ions move to the anode (positive electrode), where 2Cl$^-$ → Cl$_2$ + 2e$^-$. So option (1) puts chlorine at the wrong electrode.
Option (3) is wrong: Na$^+$ ions gain electrons; they do not lose them.
Option (4) is wrong: NCERT specifies the molten chloride, not an aqueous solution.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
A student draws two conclusions from his lab observations:
Conclusion 1: Every element with a shining surface is a metal.
Conclusion 2: Every element that conducts electricity is a metal.
Which pair of elements, taken together, disproves both conclusions?
options: Mercury and sodium
Iodine and graphite
Diamond and bromine
Gallium and caesium
questions.explanation:
To disprove Conclusion 1, we need a lustrous non-metal. Iodine fits.
To disprove Conclusion 2, we need a non-metal that conducts electricity. Graphite fits.
Mercury, sodium, gallium and caesium are all metals, so they cannot disprove either conclusion.
Diamond and bromine are non-metals, but neither is lustrous or a conductor according to NCERT.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which of the following metals does NOT give hydrogen gas when added to dilute hydrochloric acid?
options: Zinc
Iron
Copper
Magnesium
questions.explanation:
Only metals placed above hydrogen in the activity series can displace hydrogen from dilute acids.
Mg, Zn and Fe are above hydrogen, so they release H2.
Copper is below hydrogen, so it does not react with dilute HCl. NCERT notes that no bubbles form and the temperature does not change.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: The chloride ion ($Cl^-$) formed in the reaction between sodium and chlorine has the same electronic configuration as which noble gas?
options: Helium
Neon
Krypton
Argon
questions.explanation:
Chlorine (atomic number 17) has the configuration 2, 8, 7.
It gains one electron to become $Cl^-$, with configuration 2, 8, 8 (18 electrons).
Argon (atomic number 18) also has the configuration 2, 8, 8.
Neon is tempting, but neon (2, 8) matches the $Na^+$ ion, not $Cl^-$.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Gold ornaments in India are generally made of 22 carat gold. Pure gold is 24 carat. What is the approximate percentage of pure gold in a 22 carat ornament?
questions.explanation:
Given: 22 carat gold means 22 parts pure gold alloyed with 2 parts copper or silver, making 24 parts in all.
Formula: % gold = (parts of gold ÷ total parts) × 100
Substituting: % gold = (22 ÷ 24) × 100
So the percentage of gold is about 91.67%.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Diamond is a non-metal yet has very high melting and boiling points.
Gallium is a metal but would melt if held on the palm.
Since graphite conducts electricity, all allotropes of carbon conduct electricity.
Sodium is a metal yet it is soft enough to be cut with a knife.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: diamond has very high melting and boiling points, even though it is a non-metal.
(2) Correct: gallium has a very low melting point and melts on the palm.
(3) Incorrect: the allotropes of carbon differ in their properties. Graphite conducts electricity, but NCERT describes diamond only for its hardness and high melting point, so the generalisation is wrong.
(4) Correct: alkali metals such as sodium are very soft.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (metal and condition) with List-II (observation):
List-I
(a) Copper heated in air
(b) Iron filings sprinkled in a burner flame
(c) Gold heated strongly in air
(d) Potassium left in the open
List-II
(i) No reaction with oxygen
(ii) Catches fire; hence stored under kerosene
(iii) Burn vigorously
(iv) Gets coated with a black layer of copper(II) oxide
questions.explanation:
(a) Copper does not burn, but the hot metal gets coated with black CuO, so (a) matches (iv).
(b) A lump of iron does not burn on heating, but iron filings burn vigorously in a flame, so (b) matches (iii).
(c) Gold and silver do not react with oxygen even at high temperatures, so (c) matches (i).
(d) Potassium reacts so vigorously with air that it catches fire and is stored in kerosene, so (d) matches (ii).
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Copper can be obtained from $Cu_2S$ simply by heating it in air.
(ii) In the electrolysis of molten NaCl, chlorine is liberated at the cathode.
(iii) In the thermit reaction, iron is produced in the molten state because the reaction is highly exothermic.
(iv) The ores of many metals are oxides because oxygen is very reactive and very abundant on earth.
(v) Calcination of an ore is carried out in the presence of excess air.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: $2Cu_2S + 3O_2 \rightarrow 2Cu_2O + 2SO_2$, and then $2Cu_2O + Cu_2S \rightarrow 6Cu + SO_2$.
(ii) Incorrect: chlorine is liberated at the anode, while Na is deposited at the cathode.
(iii) Correct: the heat released melts the iron, which is why the reaction is used to join railway tracks.
(iv) Correct: this is NCERT's reason for oxide ores being common.
(v) Incorrect: calcination uses limited air; roasting uses excess air.
So 3 statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A copper statue kept in the open slowly loses its shiny brown surface and gets a green coating. The green substance is
options: copper sulphide
copper(II) oxide
basic copper carbonate
copper sulphate
questions.explanation:
Copper reacts slowly with moist carbon dioxide in the air.
This forms a green coat of basic copper carbonate.
Copper(II) oxide is black. It forms when copper is heated in air, so it is not the green coating.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Aluminium oxide shows amphoteric behaviour. One mole of $Al_2O_3$ reacts completely with x moles of HCl in one experiment and with y moles of NaOH in another, forming salt and water each time. What is the ratio x : y?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Reaction with acid: $Al_2O_3 + 6HCl \rightarrow 2AlCl_3 + 3H_2O$, so x = 6.
Step 2: Reaction with base: $Al_2O_3 + 2NaOH \rightarrow 2NaAlO_2 + H_2O$, so y = 2.
Step 3: x : y = 6 : 2 = 3 : 1.
The tempting option 6 : 1 wrongly assumes only 1 mole of NaOH is used.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Four metals P, Q, R and S were tested with solutions of each other's salts. The observations were:
• P in the salt solution of Q: Q is deposited
• P in the salt solution of S: no reaction
• R in the salt solution of Q: no reaction
• S in the salt solution of R: R is deposited
Which order of decreasing reactivity is fully consistent with all these observations?
options: S > P > Q > R
P > S > Q > R
S > P > R > Q
R > Q > P > S
questions.explanation:
Use the rule: if metal A displaces B, then A is more reactive than B.
(i) P displaces Q, so P > Q.
(ii) P does not displace S, so S > P.
(iii) R does not displace Q, so Q > R.
(iv) S displaces R, so S > R. This agrees with the chain.
Combining these gives S > P > Q > R.
Option (2) breaks observation (ii). Option (3) breaks observation (iii).
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (element) with List-II (electronic configuration):
List-I: (P) Potassium (Q) Calcium (R) Phosphorus (S) Sulphur
List-II: (i) 2, 8, 5 (ii) 2, 8, 8, 2 (iii) 2, 8, 6 (iv) 2, 8, 8, 1
options: P-(iv), Q-(ii), R-(i), S-(iii)
P-(ii), Q-(iv), R-(i), S-(iii)
P-(iv), Q-(ii), R-(iii), S-(i)
P-(i), Q-(iii), R-(iv), S-(ii)
questions.explanation:
Potassium has Z = 19, so its configuration is 2, 8, 8, 1, giving (iv).
Calcium has Z = 20, so its configuration is 2, 8, 8, 2, giving (ii).
Phosphorus has Z = 15, so its configuration is 2, 8, 5, giving (i).
Sulphur has Z = 16, so its configuration is 2, 8, 6, giving (iii).
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following metals react with cold water?
Potassium, sodium, calcium, magnesium, aluminium, zinc, iron, copper
questions.explanation:
Potassium and sodium react violently with cold water.
Calcium reacts with cold water less violently.
Magnesium does not react with cold water; it needs hot water.
Aluminium, zinc and iron react only with steam.
Copper does not react with water at all.
So only K, Na and Ca react with cold water, which makes 3.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: Copper sulphate solution can be safely stored in a silver container.
Statement II: Silver nitrate solution can be safely stored in a copper container.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
A solution can be stored safely only if the container metal is less reactive than the metal in the salt.
Statement I is correct. Ag is below Cu, so silver cannot displace copper.
Statement II is incorrect. Cu is above Ag, so the copper container would displace silver and get corroded:
Cu + 2AgNO3 → Cu(NO3)2 + 2Ag
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the reactions of metals with water are correct?
(i) Iron reacts with steam to form $Fe_2O_3$ and hydrogen.
(ii) Magnesium reacts with hot water to form magnesium hydroxide and hydrogen.
(iii) When 2 mol of aluminium react completely with steam, 3 mol of hydrogen are formed.
(iv) Lead does not react with cold water but reacts with steam.
(v) The reaction of potassium with cold water is so exothermic that the evolved hydrogen catches fire.
questions.explanation:
(i) Incorrect: the oxide formed is $Fe_3O_4$, as in $3Fe + 4H_2O \rightarrow Fe_3O_4 + 4H_2$.
(ii) Correct: magnesium reacts with hot water to give $Mg(OH)_2$ and $H_2$.
(iii) Correct: from $2Al + 3H_2O \rightarrow Al_2O_3 + 3H_2$, 2 mol Al give 3 mol $H_2$.
(iv) Incorrect: lead does not react with water at all, not even with steam.
(v) Correct: potassium reacts violently, and the heat ignites the hydrogen.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: An aluminium wire is clamped to a stand. A pin is fixed to its free end with wax. The wire is heated near the clamp, and after some time the pin falls off. If the aluminium wire is replaced by a lead wire of the same size, and the lead wire does not melt, what will happen?
options: The pin will fall sooner than before
The pin will fall later than before
The pin will never fall because lead does not conduct heat at all
The pin will fall after the same time because all metals conduct heat equally
questions.explanation:
The pin falls when heat travels along the wire and melts the wax at the free end.
Aluminium is a good conductor of heat. Lead is comparatively a poor conductor of heat.
Heat therefore reaches the wax more slowly through lead, so the pin falls later.
Option (3) is wrong because lead still conducts heat, only poorly. Option (4) is wrong because different metals conduct heat to different extents.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which pair of metals can evolve hydrogen gas when they react with very dilute nitric acid?
options: Copper and silver
Magnesium and manganese
Zinc and iron
Gold and platinum
questions.explanation:
HNO$_3$ normally oxidises H$_2$ to water, so hydrogen is usually not obtained.
NCERT names magnesium (Mg) and manganese (Mn) as the exceptions: they give H$_2$ with very dilute HNO$_3$.
Zinc and iron react with HNO$_3$ but give nitrogen oxides instead of H$_2$.
Copper and silver do not release H$_2$ from acids.
Gold and platinum dissolve only in aqua regia.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student places two electrodes on a dry crystal of potassium iodide in a circuit with a bulb. The bulb does not glow. What is the correct reason?
options: Potassium iodide does not contain any ions
The ions are present but cannot move because of the rigid structure of the solid
Potassium iodide is a covalent compound
The electrons in potassium iodide are free but move too slowly
questions.explanation:
Conduction of electricity requires charged particles that can move.
Solid potassium iodide does contain K$^+$ and I$^-$ ions. In the solid, however, these ions are held in a rigid structure and cannot move.
Option (1) is the tempting trap. The ions are present, but they are not mobile.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which pair of metals does NOT react with oxygen even at high temperatures?
options: Copper and iron
Zinc and lead
Magnesium and aluminium
Silver and gold
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that silver and gold do not react with oxygen even at high temperatures. This is one reason they keep their shine and are used in jewellery.
Copper forms black CuO on heating, and iron filings burn in a flame.
Magnesium burns with a dazzling white flame.
Zinc and lead get covered with an oxide layer.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Case: A student is given an ore of a moderately reactive metal M (M is not iron). When the ore is heated strongly in limited air, it gives a gas that turns lime water milky and leaves behind a white oxide. The oxide is then heated with coke, and metal M and carbon monoxide are formed.
Which option correctly identifies the ore type, the first step and the reduction reaction?
options: Sulphide ore; roasting; $ZnO + C \rightarrow Zn + CO$
Carbonate ore; roasting; $2ZnO \rightarrow 2Zn + O_2$
Sulphide ore; calcination; $ZnS + C \rightarrow Zn + CS$
Carbonate ore; calcination; $ZnO + C \rightarrow Zn + CO$
questions.explanation:
The gas turns lime water milky, so it is $CO_2$. This means the ore is a carbonate.
Heating a carbonate strongly in limited air is calcination: $ZnCO_3 \rightarrow ZnO + CO_2$. ZnO is white.
The oxide is reduced by carbon: $ZnO + C \rightarrow Zn + CO$.
Option (1) fails because a sulphide ore would release $SO_2$, which does not turn lime water milky.
Option (2) fails because ZnO is not reduced by heating alone.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Silver anklets turn black after being worn for some months. This happens because silver reacts with:
options: oxygen in the air, forming silver oxide
sulphur in the air, forming silver sulphide
moist carbon dioxide, forming silver carbonate
water vapour, forming silver hydroxide
questions.explanation:
Silver does not react with oxygen even at high temperatures, so option (1) is ruled out.
The black tarnish forms because silver reacts with sulphur present in the air.
The product is a coating of silver sulphide.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Equal small amounts of barium chloride are added to three test tubes containing water, petrol and kerosene respectively. What will most likely be observed?
options: It dissolves in all three liquids
It dissolves in petrol and kerosene but not in water
It dissolves in water but not in petrol or kerosene
It does not dissolve in any of the three liquids
questions.explanation:
Barium chloride is an ionic (electrovalent) compound.
Ionic compounds are generally soluble in water.
They are insoluble in solvents such as kerosene and petrol.
So the salt dissolves only in the test tube containing water.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
A student tested four metals, W, X, Y and Z, and recorded these results:
- W gives hydrogen with dilute HCl but does not displace zinc from zinc sulphate solution.
- X displaces zinc from zinc sulphate solution.
- Y does not react with dilute HCl but displaces silver from silver nitrate solution.
- Z reacts with none of these: dilute HCl, zinc sulphate solution or silver nitrate solution.
Which identification of the metals is consistent with these results?
options: W = Mg, X = Fe, Y = Cu, Z = Au
W = Fe, X = Mg, Y = Au, Z = Cu
W = Fe, X = Mg, Y = Cu, Z = Au
W = Cu, X = Mg, Y = Fe, Z = Au
questions.explanation:
X is above Zn, so X = Mg.
W is above H but below Zn, so W = Fe (Pb would also fit).
Y is below H but above Ag, so Y = Cu.
Z is below Ag, so Z = Au.
Option (1) fails because Mg would displace zinc.
Option (4) fails because Cu cannot release H2 from dilute HCl.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Read the following statements about ionic compounds:
(i) They are generally brittle and break into pieces when pressure is applied.
(ii) Among NaCl, LiCl, $CaCl_2$, MgCl$_2$ and CaO, calcium oxide has the highest melting point (2850 K).
(iii) They dissolve readily in kerosene and petrol.
(iv) Solid sodium chloride conducts electricity because it is made of ions.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: ionic solids are somewhat hard but brittle, and they break when pressure is applied.
(ii) Correct: CaO melts at 2850 K, far above NaCl (1074 K), CaCl$_2$ (1045 K), MgCl$_2$ (981 K) and LiCl (887 K).
(iii) Incorrect: ionic compounds are generally soluble in water but insoluble in kerosene and petrol.
(iv) Incorrect: the ions in the solid cannot move because the structure is rigid, so solid NaCl does not conduct.
Two statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Hydrogen gas is generally not evolved when a metal reacts with nitric acid.
Reason (R): Nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent. It oxidises the hydrogen produced to water and is itself reduced to an oxide of nitrogen.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Metals usually give no H$_2$ with HNO$_3$.
R is true. HNO$_3$ oxidises H$_2$ to H$_2$O and is itself reduced to N$_2$O, NO or NO$_2$.
R directly explains why no H$_2$ comes out.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Consider the reaction $3MnO_2 + 4Al \rightarrow 3Mn + 2Al_2O_3 + \text{Heat}$.
Which of the following statements about this reaction is correct?
options: $MnO_2$ is oxidised and Al is reduced
Al acts as a reducing agent and is itself oxidised to $Al_2O_3$
It is an endothermic reaction, so manganese is obtained as a solid powder
Carbon must be added for manganese to be displaced
questions.explanation:
Aluminium gains oxygen to form $Al_2O_3$, so Al is oxidised. By doing so it reduces $MnO_2$, so Al is the reducing agent. This makes (2) correct.
Option (1) is wrong: $MnO_2$ loses oxygen, so it is reduced, not oxidised.
Option (3) is wrong: the reaction is highly exothermic, so Mn is produced in the molten state.
Option (4) is wrong: no carbon is needed, because more reactive Al displaces Mn on its own.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: In the electrolytic refining of copper, which of the following statements is correct?
options: The impure copper rod is made the cathode
Soluble impurities settle below the anode as anode mud
The electrolyte is acidified copper sulphate solution, and the cathode becomes heavier during the process
Pure copper is deposited on the anode
questions.explanation:
In refining, the impure copper is the anode and a thin strip of pure copper is the cathode. This rules out (1).
Only insoluble impurities settle as anode mud. Soluble impurities go into the solution, so (2) is wrong.
The electrolyte is acidified $CuSO_4$. Pure copper deposits on the cathode, so the cathode gains mass and (3) is correct.
Copper deposits on the cathode, not the anode, so (4) is wrong.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A dull-looking piece of magnesium ribbon becomes bright and shiny after it is rubbed with sand paper. This shiny appearance is called:
options: Malleability
Metallic lustre
Sonority
Ductility
questions.explanation:
Rubbing with sand paper removes the dull surface layer and exposes the pure metal.
Metals in their pure state have a shining surface. This property is called metallic lustre.
The other options describe forming sheets, producing sound and drawing into wires, not shine.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following show a physical property that is NOT typical of their class (metal or non-metal)?
(a) Iodine having lustre
(b) Mercury being liquid at room temperature
(c) Copper being a good conductor of heat
(d) Diamond having a very high melting point
(e) Sodium being cut easily with a knife
(f) Sulphur not conducting electricity
(g) Graphite conducting electricity
questions.explanation:
(a) Atypical: iodine is a non-metal, yet it is lustrous.
(b) Atypical: metals are normally solids at room temperature.
(c) Typical: metals are good conductors of heat.
(d) Atypical: NCERT lists diamond's very high melting and boiling points as an exception for a non-metal.
(e) Atypical: metals are generally hard.
(f) Typical: non-metals are bad conductors.
(g) Atypical: graphite is the exception among non-metals.
Total atypical = 5.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: When steam is passed over red-hot iron, the products formed are:
options: $Fe(OH)_2$ and $H_2$
$Fe_2O_3$ and $O_2$
$Fe_3O_4$ and $H_2$
$FeO$ and $O_2$
questions.explanation:
Iron does not react with cold or hot water, but it reacts with steam.
The reaction is $3Fe(s) + 4H_2O(g) \rightarrow Fe_3O_4(s) + 4H_2(g)$.
So the products are $Fe_3O_4$ and hydrogen.
A hydroxide is not formed with steam, and oxygen gas is never released in this reaction.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: Iodine is a non-metal, yet it has a lustrous appearance.
Statement II: Graphite, an allotrope of carbon, is a conductor of electricity.
Choose the correct option.
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: NCERT names iodine as a non-metal that is lustrous. This is an exception to the usual properties of non-metals.
Statement II is correct: graphite is a non-metal that conducts electricity. It is the stated exception to non-metals being bad conductors.
Both statements show that elements cannot be grouped by physical properties alone.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: A vessel made of lead would heat water faster than an identical vessel made of copper.
Statement II: Lead is comparatively a poor conductor of heat, whereas copper is one of the best conductors of heat.
options: Both statements are true, and Statement II explains Statement I
Both statements are true, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is true, but Statement II is false
Statement I is false, but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
Statement II is true. NCERT names silver and copper as the best conductors of heat, and lead and mercury as comparatively poor conductors.
A better conductor passes heat from the flame to the water faster.
So a copper vessel heats water faster than a lead vessel, which makes Statement I false.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student burns a magnesium ribbon and dissolves the ash in water (solution P). She then burns sulphur powder, collects the fumes in a test tube and shakes them with water (solution Q). Which statement about her observations is correct?
options: Solution P turns blue litmus red because magnesium oxide is acidic
Solution P turns red litmus blue, while solution Q turns blue litmus red
Both P and Q turn red litmus blue
Solution Q turns red litmus blue because sulphur forms an alkali in water
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Magnesium burns to form magnesium oxide, which is a basic oxide. Its solution P is basic and turns red litmus blue.
Step 2: Sulphur, a non-metal, burns to form sulphur dioxide, which is an acidic oxide. Its solution Q is acidic and turns blue litmus red.
So metals generally give basic oxides and non-metals give acidic oxides.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A crystal of an ionic compound is pressed hard with the flat end of a hammer. What is the most likely result?
options: It flattens into a thin sheet
It can then be drawn into a thin wire
It breaks into small pieces
It melts immediately and turns into a liquid
questions.explanation:
Ionic compounds are solids and are somewhat hard because of the strong attraction between their ions.
However, they are generally brittle. They break into pieces when pressure is applied.
Flattening into sheets (malleability) and drawing into wires (ductility) are properties of metals, not ionic compounds.
The crystal will not melt, because ionic compounds have high melting points.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: During the electrolytic reduction of molten sodium chloride, what is obtained at the cathode?
options: Chlorine gas
Hydrogen gas
Sodium hydroxide
Sodium metal
questions.explanation:
The cathode is the negatively charged electrode, so it attracts the cations, $Na^+$.
At the cathode, each sodium ion gains an electron: $Na^+ + e^- \rightarrow Na$, so sodium metal is deposited.
Chlorine is liberated at the anode: $2Cl^- \rightarrow Cl_2 + 2e^-$.
The melt contains no water, so neither hydrogen nor NaOH can form.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following combinations will result in a displacement reaction?
(i) Zinc + copper sulphate solution
(ii) Copper + silver nitrate solution
(iii) Iron + zinc sulphate solution
(iv) Lead + copper chloride solution
(v) Silver + copper nitrate solution
(vi) Magnesium + iron(II) sulphate solution
questions.explanation:
A reaction occurs only if the added metal is above the metal present in the salt.
(i) Yes: Zn is above Cu.
(ii) Yes: Cu is above Ag.
(iii) No: Fe is below Zn.
(iv) Yes: Pb is above Cu.
(v) No: Ag is below Cu.
(vi) Yes: Mg is above Fe.
That gives a total of 4.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or of a metal and a non-metal.
(ii) An alloy in which one of the metals is mercury is called an amalgam.
(iii) Brass conducts electricity better than pure copper.
(iv) Solder, an alloy of lead and tin, has a low melting point.
(v) 22 carat gold contains 22 parts of pure gold alloyed with 2 parts of silver or copper.
(vi) Stainless steel is made by mixing iron with nickel and chromium.
(vii) Bronze is an alloy of copper and zinc.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: this is the definition of an alloy.
(ii) Correct: an alloy containing mercury is an amalgam.
(iii) Incorrect: alloys conduct less than pure metals, which is why copper, not brass, is used in circuits.
(iv) Correct: solder melts easily, so it is used to weld electrical wires.
(v) Correct: 22 carat gold is 22 parts gold to 2 parts silver or copper.
(vi) Correct: stainless steel is iron with nickel and chromium.
(vii) Incorrect: bronze is Cu + Sn; brass is Cu + Zn.
So 5 statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: School bells are made of metals rather than wood or plastic. Which property of metals is mainly responsible for this?
options: Ductility
High melting point
Sonority
Electrical conductivity
questions.explanation:
Metals produce a ringing sound when they strike a hard surface. This property is called sonority.
A bell must ring loudly, so it is made of a sonorous metal.
Ductility, melting point and electrical conductivity have nothing to do with producing sound.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: In the electrolytic refining of copper, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: The impure copper is made the anode.
Acidified copper sulphate solution is used as the electrolyte.
Insoluble impurities settle below the anode as anode mud.
Pure copper dissolves from the cathode and gets deposited on the anode.
questions.explanation:
Options 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The impure metal is the anode, acidified copper sulphate is the electrolyte, and insoluble impurities settle below the anode as anode mud.
Option 4 is incorrect because it reverses the process. Copper dissolves from the impure anode into the electrolyte, and an equal amount of pure copper deposits on the thin pure-copper cathode.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: Copper reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to liberate hydrogen gas.
Statement II: When an iron nail is kept in copper sulphate solution, copper is deposited on the nail.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Copper lies below hydrogen in the activity series. With dilute HCl there are no bubbles and no temperature change.
Statement II is correct. Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from $CuSO_4$ solution. Brown copper deposits on the nail.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
A student sets up three test tubes, each containing a clean iron nail:
Tube A: ordinary tap water, corked.
Tube B: boiled distilled water with a thin layer of oil on top, corked.
Tube C: anhydrous calcium chloride, corked.
After a few days, in which tube(s) will the nails show rusting?
options: Tube A only
Tube B only
Tubes A and B
Tubes B and C
questions.explanation:
Tube A: the nail is exposed to both water and dissolved air, so it rusts.
Tube B: boiling removes the dissolved air, and the oil layer stops fresh air from dissolving. With no air present, there is no rust.
Tube C: anhydrous CaCl2 absorbs moisture, so the air is dry and there is no rust.
Rusting therefore needs both air and water. Option (3) is wrong because water alone, as in tube B, does not cause rusting.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: In an activity, equal-sized clean pieces of Mg, Al, Zn and Fe are placed in separate test tubes containing the same dilute HCl. A thermometer bulb is dipped in each tube. Which order shows the decreasing rate of bubble formation (and decreasing temperature rise)?
options: Mg > Al > Zn > Fe
Al > Mg > Fe > Zn
Zn > Fe > Mg > Al
Fe > Zn > Al > Mg
questions.explanation:
A more reactive metal releases hydrogen faster and gives out more heat.
Magnesium gives the fastest bubbling and the highest temperature.
NCERT gives the reactivity order with dilute acid as Mg > Al > Zn > Fe.
Option (2) wrongly puts Al above Mg, even though Mg is above Al in the activity series.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The copper wires that carry current in our homes are covered with a coating of polyvinylchloride (PVC) or a rubber-like material.
Reason (R): Metals such as copper are good conductors of electricity, whereas PVC and rubber-like materials do not conduct electricity.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation:
A is true. Household wires carry a PVC or rubber-like coating.
R is true. Metals conduct electricity, while PVC and rubber are insulators.
The coating is used precisely because it does not conduct. It stops current from passing to our body or to nearby wires if they touch, which prevents shocks and short circuits.
So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student strikes small pieces of zinc, copper and lead with a hammer on an iron block. The pieces flatten into thin sheets. Which property of metals does this show?
options: Ductility
Malleability
Sonority
Metallic lustre
questions.explanation:
Malleability is the ability of a metal to be beaten into thin sheets.
Hammering flattened the metals into sheets, so this is malleability.
Ductility is the tempting wrong option, but it means being drawn into wires, not beaten into sheets.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: A block of iron does not burn when heated, but iron filings burn vigorously when sprinkled into the flame of a burner.
Statement II: Finely divided iron filings expose a much larger surface area to oxygen, so they combine with oxygen far more rapidly than a solid block.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true, and Statement II correctly explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are true, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is true, but Statement II is false
Statement I is false, but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
Statement I is true. NCERT notes that iron does not burn on heating, but iron filings burn vigorously in a burner flame.
Statement II is true. The metal and the oxygen are the same in both cases. Only the state of division differs.
Filings offer a far larger surface area in contact with oxygen, so oxidation becomes fast enough to burn. This is exactly why Statement I happens.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student is given a white ore of a moderately reactive metal M. She heats it strongly in a limited supply of air. She gets a metal oxide and a colourless gas that turns lime water milky. No sulphur dioxide is produced. She then heats the oxide with coke and obtains metal M and carbon monoxide. Which option correctly identifies the ore and the two steps?
options: ZnS; roasting followed by electrolytic reduction
ZnS; calcination followed by reduction with carbon
$ZnCO_3$; roasting followed by reduction with carbon
$ZnCO_3$; calcination followed by reduction with carbon
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Heating strongly in limited air, with CO$_2$ released and no SO$_2$, shows a carbonate ore. This step is calcination: ZnCO$_3$ → ZnO + CO$_2$.
Step 2: Heating the oxide with coke is carbon reduction: ZnO + C → Zn + CO.
Roasting is done in excess air on a sulphide ore and gives SO$_2$, so ZnS and roasting do not fit.
Electrolysis is needed only for highly reactive metals, not moderately reactive ones.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (metal + reagent) with List-II (observation):
List-I
(A) Magnesium + very dilute HNO$_3$
(B) Copper + dilute HCl
(C) Zinc + dilute HNO$_3$
(D) Gold + aqua regia
List-II
(i) No reaction takes place
(ii) An oxide of nitrogen (N$_2$O, NO or NO$_2$) is formed instead of H$_2$
(iii) Hydrogen gas is evolved
(iv) Metal dissolves, though it does not dissolve in either acid separately
options: A-(iii), B-(i), C-(ii), D-(iv)
A-(ii), B-(i), C-(iii), D-(iv)
A-(iii), B-(ii), C-(i), D-(iv)
A-(iv), B-(i), C-(ii), D-(iii)
questions.explanation:
(A) Mg is one of the two exceptions that give H$_2$ with very dilute HNO$_3$, so it matches (iii).
(B) Cu is below hydrogen and does not react with dilute HCl, so it matches (i).
(C) Zn is not an exception. HNO$_3$ oxidises the H$_2$ and is reduced to nitrogen oxides, so it matches (ii).
(D) Gold dissolves only in aqua regia, so it matches (iv).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about ionic compounds are correct?
(i) They exist as aggregates of oppositely charged ions rather than as molecules.
(ii) They conduct electricity in the solid state.
(iii) They are generally soluble in kerosene.
(iv) They have high boiling points.
(v) In their aqueous solution, ions move towards the opposite electrodes when current is passed.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct. Example: NaCl is made of Na$^+$ and Cl$^-$ ions, not molecules.
(ii) Incorrect. The ions are fixed in a rigid structure, so the solid does not conduct.
(iii) Incorrect. Ionic compounds are insoluble in kerosene and petrol.
(iv) Correct. The strong inter-ionic attraction needs much energy to overcome.
(v) Correct. The dissolved ions are mobile and carry current.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (metal to be obtained) with List-II (method used).
List-I:
(A) Sodium from sodium chloride
(B) Zinc from zinc carbonate
(C) Mercury from cinnabar (HgS)
(D) Manganese from manganese dioxide
List-II:
(i) Heating the ore in air alone
(ii) Electrolysis of the molten compound
(iii) Heating with aluminium powder
(iv) Calcination followed by reduction with carbon
options: A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii)
A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(ii)
A-(ii), B-(i), C-(iv), D-(iii)
A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(iii), D-(i)
questions.explanation:
A-(ii): Sodium is highly reactive, so it is obtained by electrolysis of molten NaCl.
B-(iv): Zinc carbonate is calcined to ZnO, and ZnO is then reduced with carbon.
C-(i): Mercury is low in the series. Heating HgS in air gives HgO, which on further heating gives mercury.
D-(iii): $MnO_2$ is reduced by aluminium powder in a displacement reaction.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Four metals W, X, Y and Z were added separately to four salt solutions. A tick means displacement occurred; a cross means no reaction.
W: $ZnSO_4$ ✓, $FeSO_4$ ✓, $CuSO_4$ ✓, $AgNO_3$ ✓
X: $ZnSO_4$ ✗, $FeSO_4$ ✓, $CuSO_4$ ✓, $AgNO_3$ ✓
Y: $ZnSO_4$ ✗, $FeSO_4$ ✗, $CuSO_4$ ✓, $AgNO_3$ ✓
Z: $ZnSO_4$ ✗, $FeSO_4$ ✗, $CuSO_4$ ✗, $AgNO_3$ ✓
Which conclusion is correct?
options: Reactivity order is W > X > Y > Z, and Z will liberate hydrogen from dilute HCl
Reactivity order is Z > Y > X > W, and W cannot displace hydrogen from dilute acids
Reactivity order is W > Y > X > Z, and Y lies above iron in the activity series
Reactivity order is W > X > Y > Z, and Z will not liberate hydrogen from dilute HCl
questions.explanation:
A metal that displaces more metals is more reactive.
W displaces all four, X three, Y two and Z one. So the order is W > X > Y > Z.
Z cannot displace copper but can displace silver. This places Z below copper and above silver.
Copper is already below hydrogen, so Z also lies below hydrogen. Z cannot liberate $H_2$ from dilute HCl.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student refines a block of impure copper electrolytically and observes the two electrodes after several hours. Which observation is expected?
options: The anode becomes thinner and the cathode becomes thicker
The anode becomes thicker and the cathode becomes thinner
Both electrodes become thicker
Neither electrode changes in size
questions.explanation:
The impure copper anode dissolves into the electrolyte, so it becomes thinner.
An equivalent amount of pure copper from the electrolyte deposits on the cathode, so it becomes thicker.
Metal is transferred from the anode to the cathode, so options (2), (3) and (4) are ruled out.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: A copper vessel can be used to store dilute hydrochloric acid for a short time without any evolution of hydrogen.
Statement II: Gold dissolves in aqua regia, although neither concentrated HCl nor concentrated HNO$_3$ alone can dissolve it.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Copper is below hydrogen in the activity series and does not react with dilute HCl, so no H$_2$ is formed.
Statement II is correct. NCERT states that aqua regia dissolves gold even though neither acid can do so alone.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Sodium, magnesium and aluminium cannot be obtained by heating their oxides with carbon.
Reason (R): These metals have a greater affinity for oxygen than carbon does.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT states that carbon cannot reduce the oxides of Na, Mg, Ca and Al, so these metals are obtained by electrolytic reduction.
R is true: these metals hold oxygen more strongly than carbon does.
R explains A: because the metal holds oxygen more strongly, carbon cannot pull the oxygen away from it.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: Alkali metals such as lithium, sodium and potassium have low densities and low melting points.
Statement II: Alkali metals are so hard that they cannot be cut with a knife.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: NCERT states that the alkali metals Li, Na and K have low densities and low melting points.
Statement II is incorrect: these metals are so soft that they can be cut with a knife. This makes them exceptions to the general hardness of metals.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: In the formation of $Na_2O$, one oxygen atom gains two electrons, one from each of two sodium atoms.
Statement II: In the formation of MgO, one magnesium atom transfers only one electron to an oxygen atom.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
questions.explanation:
Oxygen (2, 6) needs two electrons to complete its octet. Each Na (2, 8, 1) can give only one electron.
Statement I is therefore correct: two Na atoms each donate one electron, giving $2Na^+$ and $O^{2-}$.
Statement II is incorrect: Mg (2, 8, 2) transfers both of its valence electrons to one O atom, forming $Mg^{2+}$ and $O^{2-}$.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Aluminium and copper are commonly used to make cooking vessels.
Reason (R): Metals are good conductors of heat and have high melting points.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: aluminium and copper vessels are used widely in kitchens.
R is true: Activity 3.5 shows that metals conduct heat well and do not melt on heating.
Good heat conduction cooks food quickly, and a high melting point keeps the vessel from melting on the flame. So R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: Aluminium, iron and zinc react with steam to form metal hydroxides and hydrogen gas.
Statement II: Lead does not react with water, even in the form of steam.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. With steam, Al, Fe and Zn form metal oxides, not hydroxides. Example: $2Al + 3H_2O \rightarrow Al_2O_3 + 3H_2$.
Statement II is correct. Lead, like Cu, Ag and Au, does not react with water at all.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: To refine impure zinc, a student uses zinc sulphate solution as the electrolyte. By mistake, the block of impure zinc is connected to the negative terminal of the battery and the thin strip of pure zinc to the positive terminal. What is the most likely result?
options: Refining proceeds normally, because the electrolyte is correct
Impure zinc dissolves and pure zinc deposits on the thin strip
The impure zinc block dissolves completely and no metal deposits anywhere
The thin pure zinc strip dissolves and zinc deposits on the impure block, so no purification occurs
questions.explanation:
The electrode connected to the positive terminal is the anode, and the anode dissolves.
In this wrong set-up, the pure zinc strip is the anode, so it dissolves.
The impure block becomes the cathode, and zinc from the electrolyte deposits on it.
The impurities stay inside the block, so the metal is not purified.
Correct refining requires the impure metal to be the anode.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
A factory gives aluminium window frames an attractive coloured finish that also resists corrosion. Read the following statements about this process and related facts:
(i) In anodising, the clean aluminium article is made the cathode.
(ii) Dilute sulphuric acid is used as the electrolyte during anodising.
(iii) Oxygen evolved at the anode reacts with aluminium to make the oxide layer thicker.
(iv) The thick oxide layer formed can be dyed easily.
(v) Silver and gold, when heated strongly, form a protective oxide layer similar to that on aluminium.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
(i) Incorrect: the aluminium article is made the anode, not the cathode.
(ii) Correct: electrolysis is carried out with dilute sulphuric acid.
(iii) Correct: oxygen released at the anode reacts with aluminium and thickens the protective $Al_2O_3$ layer.
(iv) Correct: the thicker oxide layer can be dyed to give an attractive finish.
(v) Incorrect: silver and gold do not react with oxygen even at high temperatures, so they form no oxide layer.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Aqua regia, which can dissolve gold and platinum, is a freshly prepared mixture of:
options: Concentrated HCl and concentrated HNO$_3$ in the ratio 1:3
Concentrated HCl and concentrated HNO$_3$ in the ratio 3:1
Concentrated H$_2$SO$_4$ and concentrated HNO$_3$ in the ratio 3:1
Dilute HCl and dilute HNO$_3$ in the ratio 3:1
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes aqua regia ('royal water') as concentrated HCl and concentrated HNO$_3$ mixed in the ratio 3:1.
The ratio 1:3 reverses the proportions, so option (1) is wrong.
Sulphuric acid is not one of its components.
Both acids used are concentrated, not dilute.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student heats four metal samples in the apparatus used to pass steam over a metal. Which metal will show NO reaction even with steam?
options: Zinc
Aluminium
Iron
Copper
questions.explanation:
Zinc, aluminium and iron do not react with cold or hot water. They do react with steam to give a metal oxide and hydrogen.
Lead, copper, silver and gold do not react with water in any form.
So copper shows no reaction.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which one of the following metals is found in nature both in the free (native) state and in the combined state as its sulphide or oxide ores?
options: Sodium
Zinc
Copper
Aluminium
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that gold, silver, platinum and copper are found in the free state.
It also states that copper and silver occur in the combined state as sulphide or oxide ores.
Sodium and aluminium are highly reactive, so they are never found free in nature.
Zinc is moderately reactive and occurs mainly as oxide, sulphide or carbonate ores, not in the native state.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Ionic compounds conduct electricity in the molten state but not in the solid state.
(ii) Aluminium oxide reacts with sodium hydroxide to form sodium aluminate and water.
(iii) Brass conducts electricity better than pure copper.
(iv) Magnesium oxide can be reduced to magnesium by heating it with carbon.
(v) During electrolysis of molten sodium chloride, sodium is deposited at the anode.
(vi) Magnesium reacts with very dilute nitric acid to evolve hydrogen gas.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: ions are fixed in the rigid solid but move freely in the melt.
(ii) Correct: Al2O3 is amphoteric, so it reacts with NaOH to give NaAlO2 and H2O.
(iii) Incorrect: alloys conduct electricity less well than pure metals.
(iv) Incorrect: magnesium has more affinity for oxygen than carbon does, so carbon cannot reduce MgO.
(v) Incorrect: Na+ ions are reduced at the cathode, not the anode.
(vi) Correct: this is the stated exception, along with manganese.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match the observations in List-I with the property of metals they illustrate in List-II.
List-I
(A) A wire about 2 km long can be drawn from one gram of gold
(B) A pin fixed with wax to the free end of a clamped copper wire falls off when the wire is heated near the clamp
(C) A dull magnesium ribbon looks shiny after rubbing with sand paper
(D) A piece of zinc flattens into a thin sheet when struck repeatedly with a hammer
List-II
(i) Malleability
(ii) Metallic lustre
(iii) Ductility
(iv) Conduction of heat
options: A-(i), B-(iv), C-(ii), D-(iii)
A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(ii), D-(i)
A-(iii), B-(ii), C-(iv), D-(i)
A-(i), B-(ii), C-(iv), D-(iii)
questions.explanation:
(A)-(iii): Drawing a metal into thin wires is ductility. Gold is the most ductile metal.
(B)-(iv): Heat travels along the wire from the heated end and melts the wax at the far end. This shows that metals conduct heat.
(C)-(ii): Rubbing removes the dull surface layer and exposes the shine of the pure metal. This is metallic lustre.
(D)-(i): Beating a metal into thin sheets is malleability.
Do not swap ductility (wires) with malleability (sheets).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In the formation of magnesium chloride, one magnesium atom combines with two chlorine atoms.
Reason (R): A magnesium atom (2, 8, 2) loses two electrons, while each chlorine atom (2, 8, 7) needs to accept only one electron to complete its octet.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The formula of magnesium chloride is $MgCl_2$, so one Mg combines with two Cl.
R is true. Mg loses 2 electrons to become $Mg^{2+}$ (2, 8). Each Cl gains 1 electron to become $Cl^-$ (2, 8, 8).
Two electrons are released by Mg, but each Cl can take only one. So two Cl atoms are needed.
R therefore correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about ionic compounds is INCORRECT?
options: They have high melting points because a lot of energy is needed to overcome the strong inter-ionic attraction.
They conduct electricity in the solid state because they are made up of ions.
They are generally soluble in water but insoluble in kerosene and petrol.
They conduct electricity in the molten state because heat overcomes the attraction between the ions.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: strong electrostatic forces between ions must be broken, so melting points are high.
(2) Incorrect: in the solid, the ions are held in a rigid structure and cannot move, so the solid does not conduct electricity.
(3) Correct: this is the usual solubility pattern of electrovalent compounds.
(4) Correct: in the molten state the ions move freely and carry current.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Consider the following oxides:
$Al_2O_3$, $ZnO$, $Na_2O$, $CuO$, $SO_2$, $MgO$
How many of these react with both acids and bases to form salt and water?
questions.explanation:
Oxides that react with both acids and bases to give salt and water are called amphoteric oxides.
$Al_2O_3$ and $ZnO$ are amphoteric. For example, $Al_2O_3$ forms $AlCl_3$ with HCl and sodium aluminate with NaOH.
$Na_2O$, $CuO$ and $MgO$ are basic oxides.
$SO_2$ is an acidic oxide of a non-metal.
So the count is 2.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (process) with List-II (description):
List-I
(a) Roasting
(b) Calcination
(c) Anodising
(d) Galvanisation
List-II
(i) Coating iron or steel with a thin layer of zinc
(ii) Heating a carbonate ore strongly in limited air
(iii) Heating a sulphide ore strongly in excess air
(iv) Making a thicker oxide layer on aluminium by electrolysis
questions.explanation:
(a) Roasting means heating a sulphide ore in excess air: (iii).
(b) Calcination means heating a carbonate ore in limited air: (ii).
(c) Anodising makes aluminium the anode and electrolyses it with dilute sulphuric acid, thickening the oxide layer: (iv).
(d) Galvanisation coats iron or steel with zinc: (i).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Solid sodium chloride is a poor conductor of electricity.
Reason (R): Sodium chloride does not exist as molecules but as aggregates of oppositely charged ions.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Solid NaCl does not conduct electricity.
R is true. NaCl exists as aggregates of Na$^+$ and Cl$^-$ ions, not as molecules.
However, R does not explain A. The mere presence of ions cannot explain non-conduction, because the same ions conduct when the solid is molten or dissolved.
The actual reason is that the ions cannot move in the rigid solid structure.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Aluminium oxide is called an amphoteric oxide.
Reason (R): Aluminium oxide reacts with hydrochloric acid to form aluminium chloride and water, and with sodium hydroxide to form sodium aluminate and water.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT names $Al_2O_3$ and ZnO as amphoteric oxides.
R is true: $Al_2O_3 + 6HCl \rightarrow 2AlCl_3 + 3H_2O$ and $Al_2O_3 + 2NaOH \rightarrow 2NaAlO_2 + H_2O$.
An amphoteric oxide is defined as one that reacts with both acids and bases to give salt and water. R describes exactly this behaviour, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
With reference to the experiment on the conditions needed for rusting of iron:
Statement I: The water used in one test tube is boiled and covered with a layer of oil so that the nail is in contact with water but not with air.
Statement II: Anhydrous calcium chloride is placed in another test tube because it absorbs oxygen from the air.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Boiling removes the dissolved air, and the oil layer prevents air from dissolving again.
Statement II is incorrect. Anhydrous CaCl2 absorbs moisture (water vapour), not oxygen. This keeps the air in that tube dry.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about solid sodium chloride is correct?
options: It exists as discrete NaCl molecules held together by weak forces.
It exists as aggregates of oppositely charged $Na^+$ and $Cl^-$ ions held by strong electrostatic forces.
It is formed by the sharing of an electron pair between sodium and chlorine.
It contains neutral sodium and chlorine atoms arranged alternately.
questions.explanation:
Sodium transfers one electron to chlorine, forming $Na^+$ and $Cl^-$.
These oppositely charged ions are held together by strong electrostatic forces of attraction.
NCERT stresses that sodium chloride does not exist as molecules but as aggregates of ions.
Sharing of electrons describes covalent bonding, not the electron transfer that forms NaCl.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Naturally occurring elements or compounds in the earth's crust are called minerals. A mineral from which a metal can be extracted profitably, because it contains a very high percentage of that metal, is called:
options: Gangue
An ore
Anode mud
An alloy
questions.explanation:
NCERT says that at some places minerals contain a very high percentage of a particular metal, so the metal can be profitably extracted from them. Such minerals are called ores.
Gangue is the impurity, such as soil and sand, that comes mixed with the ore.
Anode mud is the insoluble impurity left at the bottom of the anode during electrolytic refining.
An alloy is a man-made homogeneous mixture.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Four metals P, Q, R and S were tested with water:
P reacts violently with cold water, and the hydrogen evolved catches fire.
Q reacts less violently with cold water and starts floating.
R does not react with cold or hot water but reacts with steam to form an oxide and hydrogen.
S does not react even with steam.
Which set gives the most likely identities of P, Q, R and S?
options: P – Sodium, Q – Calcium, R – Iron, S – Copper
P – Calcium, Q – Sodium, R – Copper, S – Iron
P – Sodium, Q – Magnesium, R – Copper, S – Iron
P – Potassium, Q – Aluminium, R – Calcium, S – Zinc
questions.explanation:
P: sodium reacts so exothermically with cold water that the hydrogen evolved catches fire.
Q: calcium reacts less violently, and the hydrogen bubbles stick to it and make it float. Magnesium reacts only with hot water, so it does not fit Q.
R: iron reacts only with steam, forming Fe3O4 and H2.
S: copper does not react with water at all.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A galvanised iron bucket does not rust even after its zinc coating gets scratched at a few places.
Reason (R): Zinc is more reactive than iron, so zinc reacts in preference to the exposed iron.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT states that a galvanised article stays protected even if the zinc coating is broken.
R is true. Zinc lies above iron in the activity series.
R also explains A. Because zinc is more reactive, it corrodes in preference to iron, so the exposed iron is still protected.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Hydrogen gas is generally not evolved when a metal reacts with nitric acid.
Reason (R): Nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent that oxidises the hydrogen produced to water and is itself reduced to oxides of nitrogen such as $N_2O$, NO or $NO_2$.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation:
A is true. Metals reacting with $HNO_3$ usually do not give $H_2$ gas. The exceptions are magnesium and manganese, which give $H_2$ with very dilute $HNO_3$.
R is true. $HNO_3$ is a strong oxidising agent. It oxidises any $H_2$ formed to water and is itself reduced to $N_2O$, NO or $NO_2$.
R directly explains why no hydrogen is collected, so R is the correct explanation of A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student puts small pieces of four metals in cold water, then in hot water, and finally passes steam over the ones that have still not reacted. Which metal will react only in the last step, that is, only with steam?
options: Magnesium
Calcium
Iron
Copper
questions.explanation:
Magnesium does not react with cold water, but it reacts with hot water. So it does not wait for steam.
Calcium reacts with cold water, though less violently than sodium.
Iron, like aluminium and zinc, reacts with neither cold nor hot water. It reacts only with steam: $3Fe + 4H_2O \rightarrow Fe_3O_4 + 4H_2$.
Copper does not react with water at all, not even with steam.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about electrolytic refining is INCORRECT?
options: Metals such as zinc, tin, nickel, silver and gold can also be refined electrolytically.
Soluble impurities in the anode deposit on the cathode along with the pure metal.
Electrolytic refining is the most widely used method for refining impure metals.
The electrolyte is a solution of a salt of the metal being refined.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: NCERT lists copper, zinc, tin, nickel, silver and gold as metals refined electrolytically.
(2) Incorrect: soluble impurities go into the solution. Only the pure metal deposits on the cathode, which is why the cathode metal is pure.
(3) Correct: NCERT calls it the most widely used refining method.
(4) Correct: a solution of the metal salt is used as the electrolyte.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: In an activity to study rusting, a clean iron nail is placed in test tube B containing boiled distilled water with about 1 mL of oil poured over it, and the tube is corked. What is the purpose of boiling the water and adding the oil layer?
options: To make sure the nail is exposed to dry air only
To remove dissolved air from the water and stop air from dissolving in it again
To supply extra oxygen to the nail so that it rusts faster
To absorb any moisture present in the test tube
questions.explanation:
Boiling drives out the air dissolved in the water.
The oil floats on the water and stops fresh air from dissolving in it, so the nail in tube B is exposed to water only.
Option (1) describes tube C, where anhydrous calcium chloride keeps the air dry. Option (4) is also the job of calcium chloride, not oil.
The nail in B does not rust, which shows that water alone cannot cause rusting.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A piece of calcium placed in water starts floating after some time.
Reason (R): Bubbles of hydrogen gas formed during the reaction stick to the surface of the calcium.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: calcium reacts with cold water, and the piece rises to the surface and floats.
R is true: the hydrogen bubbles produced cling to the metal surface.
These bubbles make the metal buoyant, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Workers join broken railway tracks by igniting a mixture of two substances. Molten iron is produced and fills the gap. Which pair of reactants is used in this thermit process?
options: Iron(III) oxide and aluminium powder
Iron(III) oxide and carbon (coke)
Manganese dioxide and aluminium powder
Zinc oxide and carbon
questions.explanation:
The thermit reaction is Fe$_2$O$_3$ + 2Al → 2Fe(l) + Al$_2$O$_3$ + heat.
The reaction gives out so much heat that the iron formed is molten. This molten iron is used to join railway tracks and cracked machine parts.
MnO$_2$ with Al is also a displacement reaction, but it gives manganese, not iron.
Carbon reduction (as with ZnO) is not the thermit process.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Four test tubes contain dilute hydrochloric acid. Pieces of zinc, iron, copper and aluminium are added, one metal to each tube. In which tube will NO gas bubbles be seen and the temperature stay unchanged?
options: Tube with zinc
Tube with iron
Tube with aluminium
Tube with copper
questions.explanation:
Copper lies below hydrogen in the activity series, so it cannot displace hydrogen from dilute HCl.
In the copper tube there are no bubbles and no rise in temperature.
Zinc, iron and aluminium lie above hydrogen. They react and release H$_2$.
Iron reacts slowly, but it does still give bubbles.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: In India, ornaments are generally made of 22 carat gold, in which 22 parts of pure gold are alloyed with 2 parts of copper or silver. What mass of pure gold is present in a 20 g bangle of 22 carat gold?
questions.explanation:
Given: mass of bangle = 20 g; 22 carat means 22 parts gold in 24 parts total.
Formula: mass of pure gold = (22/24) × total mass.
Substituting: (22/24) × 20 = 18.33 g.
So the bangle contains about 18.33 g of pure gold. 1.67 g is the mass of the copper or silver, not the gold.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (part of the electrolytic refining set-up for copper) with List-II (what it is):
List-I
(P) Anode
(Q) Cathode
(R) Electrolyte
(S) Anode mud
List-II
(i) Acidified copper sulphate solution
(ii) Insoluble impurities
(iii) Impure copper
(iv) Thin strip of pure copper
options: P-(iv), Q-(iii), R-(i), S-(ii)
P-(iii), Q-(iv), R-(ii), S-(i)
P-(iii), Q-(iv), R-(i), S-(ii)
P-(i), Q-(iv), R-(iii), S-(ii)
questions.explanation:
P (Anode) = impure copper (iii), because it is the metal to be purified.
Q (Cathode) = thin strip of pure copper (iv), on which pure copper deposits.
R (Electrolyte) = acidified copper sulphate solution (i).
S (Anode mud) = insoluble impurities (ii) that settle below the anode.
Option (1) swaps the anode and cathode.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student adds a clean magnesium ribbon to dilute hydrochloric acid. Brisk effervescence is seen, and the gas burns with a pop sound when a burning splinter is brought near it. The gas evolved is:
options: Oxygen
Chlorine
Hydrogen
Carbon dioxide
questions.explanation:
A metal reacts with a dilute acid to give a salt and hydrogen gas.
Here the reaction is Mg + 2HCl → MgCl$_2$ + H$_2$.
Hydrogen burns with a pop sound, which confirms the gas.
Chlorine is not released, because the chlorine stays in the salt MgCl$_2$. Carbon dioxide would need a carbonate, and no carbonate is present.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) All metals have the same hardness.
(ii) Gold is the most ductile metal.
(iii) Mercury is comparatively a poor conductor of heat.
(iv) Household electric wires are coated with PVC because the metal inside conducts electricity.
(v) Gold and silver are the most malleable metals.
questions.explanation:
(i) Incorrect: metals are generally hard, but hardness varies from metal to metal. Sodium, for example, can be cut with a knife.
(ii) Correct: gold is the most ductile metal.
(iii) Correct: lead and mercury are comparatively poor conductors of heat.
(iv) Correct: the metal conducts electricity, so the wire is given a PVC or rubber-like coating.
(v) Correct: gold and silver are the most malleable metals.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Three unknown substances were tested:
X: brittle white solid, melts above 1000 K, does not conduct as a solid but conducts when molten, dissolves in water.
Y: shiny solid, can be hammered into sheets, conducts electricity both as a solid and when molten.
Z: soft solid, melts at about 350 K, dissolves in kerosene, does not conduct as a solid or when molten.
Which conclusion is correct?
options: Y is the ionic compound because it conducts electricity in both states
Z is the ionic compound because it dissolves in an organic solvent
X is the ionic compound because it shows high melting point, brittleness and conduction only when its ions become mobile
X and Z are both ionic compounds because neither conducts as a solid
questions.explanation:
X fits every ionic property: it is brittle, has a high melting point, is soluble in water and conducts only when molten.
Y is lustrous, malleable and conducts as a solid. These are metallic properties, not ionic ones.
Z has a low melting point, dissolves in kerosene and never conducts. It cannot be ionic, because an ionic compound would conduct when molten.
Non-conduction as a solid alone does not make Z ionic, so option (4) fails.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student places the two electrodes of a bulb circuit into samples of sodium chloride. In which of the following cases will the bulb NOT glow?
options: Sodium chloride dissolved in water
Sodium chloride heated until it melts
Dry crystals of solid sodium chloride
A concentrated solution of sodium chloride in water
questions.explanation:
Electricity passes only when charged particles can move.
In water and in the molten state, the $Na^+$ and $Cl^-$ ions are free to move towards the opposite electrodes. So options (1), (2) and (4) all conduct.
In solid crystals, the ions are held in a rigid structure and cannot move. So solid NaCl does not conduct and the bulb does not glow.
The ions are present in the solid, but they are not mobile.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Zinc blende (ZnS) is heated strongly in the presence of excess air to convert it into zinc oxide. This process is called:
options: Calcination
Roasting
Electrolytic refining
Enrichment
questions.explanation:
Heating a sulphide ore strongly in excess air to form the oxide is called roasting.
The reaction is $2ZnS + 3O_2 \rightarrow 2ZnO + 2SO_2$.
Calcination is the tempting wrong option. It is used for carbonate ores and is done in limited air.
Electrolytic refining purifies an impure metal, and enrichment removes gangue; neither converts ZnS to ZnO.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Sodium and potassium are stored immersed in kerosene oil.
