Reason (R): Sodium and potassium react so vigorously with oxygen that they catch fire if kept in the open.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Sodium and potassium are kept under kerosene.
R is true. These metals react so vigorously with oxygen that they catch fire in the open.
Kerosene keeps air and moisture away from the metal. This prevents accidental fires, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Read the data: boiling points of NaCl, LiCl, CaCl$_2$ and CaO are 1686 K, 1600 K, 1900 K and 3120 K respectively; melting points of NaCl and LiCl are 1074 K and 887 K.
Statement I: Among these compounds, CaO has the highest boiling point.
Statement II: LiCl has a higher melting point than NaCl.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. CaO boils at 3120 K, which is higher than 1900 K, 1686 K and 1600 K.
Statement II is incorrect. LiCl melts at 887 K, which is lower than the 1074 K of NaCl.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Lead, though low in the activity series, lies above hydrogen and can displace hydrogen from dilute hydrochloric acid
Zinc can displace iron from iron(II) sulphate solution and also hydrogen from dilute sulphuric acid
Since copper cannot displace hydrogen from dilute acids, it cannot displace any metal from its salt solution
Magnesium reacts with very dilute nitric acid to give hydrogen gas
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: Pb is above [H] in the activity series.
(2) Correct: Zn is above both Fe and H.
(3) Incorrect: Cu is below H but above Hg, Ag and Au, so it can displace silver from AgNO3, for example. Not displacing hydrogen does not mean it cannot displace any metal.
(4) Correct: NCERT states that Mg and Mn give H2 with very dilute HNO3.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A galvanised iron article remains protected from rusting even if its zinc coating gets broken.
Reason (R): Zinc is less reactive than iron.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT states that a galvanised article stays protected even when the zinc coating is broken.
R is false: zinc lies above iron in the activity series, so zinc is MORE reactive than iron.
Because zinc is more reactive, it reacts in preference to iron, and this is why the exposed iron is still protected.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: In the electrolytic refining of copper, which of the following is used as the cathode?
options: A block of impure copper
A thin strip of pure copper
A graphite rod
A plate of zinc
questions.explanation:
In electrolytic refining, the impure metal is made the anode and a thin strip of the pure metal is made the cathode.
For copper, pure copper deposits on this thin strip of pure copper.
Impure copper is the anode, not the cathode.
Graphite and zinc are not used as the cathode in this process.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (element) with List-II (exceptional property).
List-I:
(P) Mercury
(Q) Diamond
(R) Sodium
(S) Graphite
List-II:
(i) Hardest natural substance known
(ii) Conducts electricity though a non-metal
(iii) Metal that is liquid at room temperature
(iv) Metal soft enough to be cut with a knife
options: P-(iii), Q-(i), R-(iv), S-(ii)
P-(iv), Q-(ii), R-(iii), S-(i)
P-(iii), Q-(ii), R-(iv), S-(i)
P-(i), Q-(iii), R-(ii), S-(iv)
questions.explanation:
P: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature, so it matches (iii).
Q: Diamond is the hardest natural substance known, so it matches (i).
R: Sodium is an alkali metal soft enough to be cut with a knife, so it matches (iv).
S: Graphite is a non-metal that conducts electricity, so it matches (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (metal) with List-II (method by which it is usually obtained) and choose the correct option.
List-I:
(P) Potassium
(Q) Zinc
(R) Mercury
(S) Gold
List-II:
(i) Found in native state
(ii) Heating the sulphide ore alone in air
(iii) Electrolysis of molten compound
(iv) Reduction of oxide using carbon
options: P-(iv), Q-(iii), R-(i), S-(ii)
P-(iii), Q-(ii), R-(iv), S-(i)
P-(iii), Q-(iv), R-(ii), S-(i)
P-(i), Q-(iv), R-(ii), S-(iii)
questions.explanation:
P - (iii): Potassium is at the top of the activity series, so it is extracted by electrolysis.
Q - (iv): Zinc is in the middle of the series; its ore is converted to ZnO, which is reduced with carbon.
R - (ii): Mercury is low in the series. Cinnabar (HgS) is heated in air to give HgO, which on further heating gives Hg.
S - (i): Gold is found in the native state.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: A magnesium ribbon dipped in zinc sulphate solution gets coated with zinc metal.
Statement II: A metal can displace another metal from its salt solution only if it lies below that metal in the activity series.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Mg lies above Zn in the activity series, so $Mg + ZnSO_4 \rightarrow MgSO_4 + Zn$ takes place. The zinc deposits on the ribbon.
Statement II is incorrect. It reverses the rule. A metal displaces another only if it is more reactive, which means it lies above that metal in the series.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: An alloy is called an amalgam when one of the metals in it is:
options: tin
mercury
copper
lead
questions.explanation:
An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or of a metal and a non-metal.
If one of the metals in the alloy is mercury, the alloy is called an amalgam.
Alloys of tin, copper or lead, such as bronze, brass and solder, are not amalgams unless mercury is present.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student places a clean iron nail in copper sulphate solution in test tube X. She places a clean copper wire in iron sulphate solution in test tube Y. Which observation would she record after about 20 minutes?
options: X: a brownish coating forms on the nail and the blue solution fades towards pale green; Y: no visible change
X: no visible change; Y: a grey coating forms on the wire and the pale green solution turns blue
Both X and Y: the metal gets coated and the solution changes colour
Both X and Y: no visible change, because neither metal reacts with salt solutions
questions.explanation:
Iron is above copper in the activity series, so iron displaces copper: $Fe + CuSO_4 \rightarrow FeSO_4 + Cu$.
The displaced copper deposits on the nail as a brownish coating. As blue $CuSO_4$ is used up and pale green $FeSO_4$ forms, the solution colour fades.
Copper is less reactive than iron, so it cannot displace iron from $FeSO_4$. Tube Y therefore shows no change.
Option (2) wrongly assumes that copper is the more reactive metal.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Zinc coating protects iron very well in buckets and roofing sheets. Yet tin, not zinc, is used to coat the inside of iron cans that store food such as fruit juices and pickles. Which reason best explains this choice?
options: Zinc is more reactive than tin, so it could react with acidic food contents and contaminate the food
Tin is more reactive than zinc, so it gives better protection to the iron
Zinc cannot form a protective layer on iron, while tin can
Tin, being a non-metal, does not conduct heat into the food
questions.explanation:
Zinc lies high in the reactivity series and reacts readily with acids.
Acidic food in contact with a zinc coating could react with it, forming zinc compounds that spoil the food.
Tin is less reactive than zinc, so it is safer for food.
Option (2) reverses the reactivity order. Option (3) contradicts galvanisation. Option (4) is wrong because tin is a metal.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: An electrician uses pure copper wires for house wiring and joins them using solder. Which of the following statements correctly explains these choices?
options: Solder has a higher melting point than lead and tin, so the joint does not melt when current flows
Brass would be better than copper for wiring because alloys conduct electricity better than pure metals
Alloys have lower electrical conductivity and lower melting point than pure metals, so copper suits wiring and solder melts easily for joining
Solder is an amalgam of lead and mercury, which makes it a good conductor
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that the electrical conductivity and melting point of an alloy are lower than those of pure metals.
(1) Wrong: solder has a low melting point, which is exactly why it is used for joining.
(2) Wrong: brass is not a good conductor, so pure copper is used in circuits.
(3) Correct: copper conducts well, and solder melts easily to join wires.
(4) Wrong: solder is lead + tin. An amalgam is an alloy that contains mercury.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
A sample of impure copper contains small amounts of zinc, iron, silver and gold. It is refined electrolytically using acidified copper sulphate solution.
Statement I: The zinc and iron impurities pass into the solution as ions.
Statement II: The silver and gold impurities collect in the anode mud.
Choose the correct option.
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Zinc and iron are above copper in the activity series. They dissolve from the anode along with copper and remain in the solution as soluble impurities, so Statement I is correct.
Silver and gold are below copper and do not dissolve. They fall as insoluble impurities into the anode mud, so Statement II is correct.
Only copper deposits on the cathode.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: When a copper strip is heated strongly in air, its surface gets coated with a black layer. What is this black substance?
options: Basic copper carbonate
Copper(II) oxide, CuO
Copper sulphide
Copper(II) hydroxide
questions.explanation:
Heated copper does not burn. It combines with oxygen of the air: $2Cu + O_2 \rightarrow 2CuO$.
Copper(II) oxide is black, so it forms the black coating.
Basic copper carbonate is the green coat that forms slowly when copper is exposed to moist carbon dioxide. It does not form on heating.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student burns a magnesium ribbon, collects the ash and dissolves it in water (Solution X). She then burns sulphur powder, collects the fumes in a test tube and shakes them with water (Solution Y). Which observation is correct when both solutions are tested with litmus paper?
options: X turns blue litmus red; Y turns red litmus blue
Both X and Y turn blue litmus red
X turns red litmus blue; Y turns blue litmus red
Both X and Y turn red litmus blue
questions.explanation:
Magnesium burns to form magnesium oxide. This is a metal oxide, so it is basic, and its solution X turns red litmus blue.
Sulphur burns to form sulphur dioxide. This is a non-metal oxide, so it is acidic, and its solution Y turns blue litmus red.
Option (1) swaps the results. Options (2) and (4) wrongly treat both oxides as the same type.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following metals are covered with a thin protective oxide layer at ordinary temperature, which prevents further oxidation?
Magnesium, aluminium, zinc, lead, gold, silver, sodium
questions.explanation:
Magnesium, aluminium, zinc and lead: NCERT says their surfaces are covered with a thin protective oxide layer at ordinary temperature.
Gold and silver: they do not react with oxygen at all, so no oxide layer forms.
Sodium: it is not protected by an oxide layer. It reacts so vigorously that it is stored in kerosene.
So the count is 4.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the electrolytic refining of copper.
(i) Impure copper is made the anode.
(ii) A thin strip of pure copper is made the cathode.
(iii) Acidified copper sulphate solution is used as the electrolyte.
(iv) Insoluble impurities pass into the solution.
(v) Soluble impurities settle below the anode as anode mud.
How many of these statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the impure metal is always made the anode.
(ii) Correct: pure copper is deposited on a thin pure strip used as the cathode.
(iii) Correct: the electrolyte is acidified copper sulphate solution.
(iv) Incorrect: it is the SOLUBLE impurities that go into the solution.
(v) Incorrect: the INSOLUBLE impurities settle down as anode mud.
So 3 statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Stainless steel is hard and does not rust. It is obtained by mixing iron with:
options: zinc and tin
copper and zinc
nickel and chromium
lead and tin
questions.explanation:
Stainless steel forms when iron is mixed with nickel and chromium.
This alloy is hard and resists rusting.
Copper with zinc gives brass, and lead with tin gives solder.
Zinc is used for galvanising, not for making stainless steel.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A galvanised iron sheet is protected from rusting even if its zinc coating gets scratched.
Reason (R): Zinc is more reactive than iron.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT states that a galvanised article is protected even when the zinc coating is broken.
R is true. Zinc lies above iron in the activity series.
R explains A: zinc, being more reactive, gets oxidised in preference to iron. This keeps the exposed iron from rusting.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Aluminium articles are anodised to make them more resistant to corrosion.
Reason (R): During anodising, the clean aluminium article is made the cathode and electrolysed with dilute sulphuric acid.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Anodising makes the protective $Al_2O_3$ layer thicker, which improves resistance to corrosion. This layer can also be dyed.
R is false. In anodising, the aluminium article is made the anode, not the cathode. The oxygen released at the anode reacts with aluminium to thicken the oxide layer.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (metal) with List-II (method by which it is usually obtained).
List-I:
(a) Sodium
(b) Zinc
(c) Mercury
(d) Gold
List-II:
(i) Found in the native (free) state
(ii) Heating its sulphide ore in air alone
(iii) Electrolysis of its molten chloride
(iv) Reduction of its oxide with carbon
questions.explanation:
(a) Sodium is highly reactive, and carbon cannot reduce its compounds. It is obtained by electrolysis of molten NaCl, so (a)-(iii).
(b) Zinc is of medium reactivity, so ZnO is reduced by carbon, giving (b)-(iv).
(c) Mercury is of low reactivity. Heating cinnabar (HgS) in air gives HgO, which decomposes on further heating, so (c)-(ii).
(d) Gold is found free in nature, so (d)-(i).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match each metal in List-I with the method by which it is obtained in List-II.
List-I:
(a) Mercury
(b) Zinc
(c) Sodium
(d) Gold
List-II:
(i) Electrolysis of the molten chloride
(ii) Found in the native state
(iii) Reduction of its oxide with carbon
(iv) Heating its sulphide ore in air alone
options: a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii
a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii
a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii
a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv
questions.explanation:
(a) Mercury is low in the series. Cinnabar (HgS) heated in air gives HgO, which on further heating gives Hg. So a-iv.
(b) Zinc is in the middle of the series. ZnO is reduced by carbon: ZnO + C → Zn + CO. So b-iii.
(c) Sodium is high in the series. It is obtained by electrolysis of molten NaCl. So c-i.
(d) Gold is the least reactive and occurs native. So d-ii.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Four metals P, Q, R and S are tested with water:
P reacts with cold water; the hydrogen does not catch fire and the metal floats.
Q reacts violently with cold water and the hydrogen evolved catches fire.
R reacts neither with cold nor hot water, but reacts with steam.
S does not react with cold water but reacts with hot water and floats.
The correct decreasing order of reactivity is:
options: P > Q > S > R
Q > P > S > R
Q > S > P > R
Q > P > R > S
questions.explanation:
Q behaves like Na or K, reacting violently with cold water, so it is the most reactive.
P behaves like Ca, reacting with cold water less violently.
S behaves like Mg, which needs hot water.
R behaves like Al, Fe or Zn, which need steam, so it is the least reactive.
The order is Q > P > S > R.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: What is the electronic configuration of the magnesium ion ($Mg^{2+}$) formed when magnesium reacts with chlorine?
questions.explanation:
Magnesium (atomic number 12) has the configuration 2, 8, 2.
It loses its two outermost (M shell) electrons to form $Mg^{2+}$.
The L shell then becomes the outermost shell, giving 2, 8, which is a stable octet like neon.
2, 8, 2 is the neutral atom, not the ion.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): No change is seen when a copper wire is kept in iron(II) sulphate solution.
Reason (R): Copper is less reactive than iron.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Copper cannot displace iron from FeSO4, so the solution stays green and the wire stays unchanged.
R is true. Cu lies below Fe in the activity series.
A metal displaces another metal from its salt solution only if it is more reactive. Copper is less reactive, so no reaction occurs. R therefore correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which pair of metals are the best conductors of heat?
options: Lead and mercury
Iron and aluminium
Silver and copper
Gold and zinc
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that silver and copper are the best conductors of heat.
Lead and mercury are comparatively poor conductors of heat, so option (1) is the opposite case.
Iron, aluminium, gold and zinc conduct heat, but they are not named as the best conductors.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) The electrical conductivity of an alloy is lower than that of the pure metals in it.
(ii) Solder is used for joining electrical wires because of its low melting point.
(iii) Pure iron is widely used for construction because it is very hard.
(iv) 24 carat gold is preferred for ornaments because it is the hardest form of gold.
(v) An alloy is a homogeneous mixture.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct. Brass and bronze conduct electricity less well than copper.
(ii) Correct. Solder, an alloy of Pb and Sn, has a low melting point.
(iii) Incorrect. Pure iron is very soft and stretches easily when hot, so it is never used pure.
(iv) Incorrect. 24 carat gold is very soft, which is why 22 carat gold is used for ornaments.
(v) Correct. An alloy is a homogeneous mixture.
So 3 statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the occurrence of metals is incorrect?
options: The earth's crust is the major source of metals.
Seawater contains soluble salts such as sodium chloride and magnesium chloride.
Every mineral is an ore, because every mineral contains a metal.
Ores mined from the earth usually contain impurities like soil and sand, called gangue.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: NCERT names the earth's crust as the major source of metals.
(2) Correct: seawater contains soluble salts such as NaCl and MgCl$_2$.
(3) Incorrect: only those minerals from which a metal can be extracted profitably are ores. So all ores are minerals, but not all minerals are ores.
(4) Correct: soil, sand and similar impurities in a mined ore are called gangue.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following metals will liberate hydrogen gas when added to dilute hydrochloric acid?
Zinc, Copper, Iron, Silver, Aluminium, Magnesium, Gold, Mercury
questions.explanation:
Only metals placed above hydrogen in the activity series can displace hydrogen from dilute acids.
Above H: Zn, Fe, Al, Mg. These 4 release H$_2$.
Below H: Cu, Hg, Ag, Au. These do not react with dilute HCl.
Total = 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Consider the formation of sodium oxide ($Na_2O$) and magnesium oxide ($MgO$) by transfer of electrons (Na = 11, Mg = 12, O = 8). How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) In $Na_2O$, each of the two sodium atoms transfers one electron to the same oxygen atom.
(ii) In $MgO$, both the cation and the anion have the electronic configuration 2, 8.
(iii) The total number of electrons transferred to form one formula unit of $Na_2O$ equals that for one formula unit of $MgO$.
(iv) The oxide ion has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 8.
(v) The $Na^+$ ion contains 11 protons and 10 electrons.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: O (2, 6) needs 2 electrons. It gets one from each Na atom.
(ii) Correct: $Mg^{2+}$ is 2, 8, and $O^{2-}$ is also 2, 8. Both match neon.
(iii) Correct: 2 electrons are transferred in $Na_2O$ (1 + 1) and 2 in $MgO$.
(iv) Incorrect: $O^{2-}$ has 10 electrons, so its configuration is 2, 8, not 2, 8, 8.
(v) Correct: losing an electron does not change the nucleus. So $Na^+$ has 11 protons and 10 electrons.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Lustre is generally a property of metals. Which non-metal is an exception because it is lustrous?
options: Sulphur
Oxygen
Carbon (coal)
Iodine
questions.explanation:
Metallic lustre means having a shining surface, which is typical of metals.
NCERT points out that iodine is a non-metal but is lustrous.
Sulphur and coal are dull solids, and oxygen is a gas.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: In an activity, equal-sized clean pieces of magnesium, aluminium, zinc, iron and copper were added separately to test tubes containing dilute hydrochloric acid. In which test tube were no gas bubbles seen and no temperature change recorded?
options: Magnesium
Zinc
Iron
Copper
questions.explanation:
Metals above hydrogen in the activity series displace hydrogen from dilute acids: Metal + dilute acid → salt + hydrogen.
Mg, Al, Zn and Fe all lie above hydrogen, so they react and give bubbles of $H_2$. Magnesium reacts fastest and is the most exothermic.
Copper lies below hydrogen, so it does not react with dilute HCl. No bubbles form and the temperature stays the same.
Iron reacts slowly but still gives some bubbles, so it is not the right choice.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: An old copper statue in a park has lost its shiny brown surface and has a green coating. Which substance forms this green coating?
options: Copper(II) oxide
Basic copper carbonate
Copper sulphate
Copper sulphide
questions.explanation:
Copper slowly reacts with moist carbon dioxide in the air.
The green substance formed is basic copper carbonate.
Copper(II) oxide is black. It forms when copper is heated in air, not in slow atmospheric corrosion.
Copper sulphate and copper sulphide are not the green coat that NCERT describes.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Three corked test tubes P, Q and R each contain clean iron nails.
P has ordinary tap water.
Q has boiled distilled water with a thin layer of oil on top.
R has anhydrous calcium chloride.
After a few days, in which tube(s) will the nails be found rusted?
options: P and Q
Q and R
Only P
P, Q and R
questions.explanation:
Rusting needs both air (oxygen) and water.
P: the nails are exposed to both air and water, so they rust.
Q: boiling removes dissolved air, and the oil layer stops fresh air dissolving. There is water but no air, so no rust.
R: anhydrous calcium chloride absorbs moisture. There is dry air but no water, so no rust.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(a) Copper heated in air
(b) Aluminium oxide treated with sodium hydroxide
(c) Potassium oxide added to water
(d) Sulphur burnt and fumes dissolved in water
List-II
(i) Sodium aluminate and water
(ii) Black copper(II) oxide
(iii) Solution that turns blue litmus red
(iv) Alkali KOH formed
questions.explanation:
(a)-(ii): $2Cu + O_2 \rightarrow 2CuO$, which is black.
(b)-(i): $Al_2O_3 + 2NaOH \rightarrow 2NaAlO_2 + H_2O$, giving sodium aluminate and water.
(c)-(iv): $K_2O + H_2O \rightarrow 2KOH$, an alkali.
(d)-(iii): sulphur dioxide dissolves to give an acidic solution, which turns blue litmus red.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A metal M shows no change in cold or hot water. When steam is passed over the heated metal, a gas that burns with a pop sound is released, and a white oxide is left behind. This oxide dissolves both in dilute HCl and in NaOH solution, forming a salt and water in each case. M is most likely:
options: Magnesium
Iron
Aluminium
Copper
questions.explanation:
Reacting only with steam narrows M to Al, Fe or Zn.
The gas that burns with a pop is hydrogen: $2Al + 3H_2O \rightarrow Al_2O_3 + 3H_2$.
An oxide that reacts with both acid and base is amphoteric, and $Al_2O_3$ is amphoteric.
Iron is ruled out because $Fe_3O_4$ is not amphoteric.
Magnesium is ruled out because it reacts with hot water.
Copper is ruled out because it does not react with steam.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Copper does not give hydrogen gas when added to dilute hydrochloric acid.
Reason (R): Copper lies below hydrogen in the activity series.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation:
A is true. When copper is placed in dilute HCl, no bubbles form and the temperature does not change, so no reaction occurs.
R is true. In the activity series, Cu comes after [H].
Only metals above hydrogen can displace hydrogen from dilute acids. Copper is below hydrogen, so it cannot release $H_2$. R therefore correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Sodium and potassium are stored immersed in kerosene oil in the laboratory. Why?
options: They dissolve in water but not in kerosene, so kerosene keeps them dry
Kerosene slowly converts them into their oxides, which are safer
They react so vigorously with oxygen that they can catch fire in the open
They are liquids at room temperature and need a liquid container
questions.explanation:
Potassium and sodium are highly reactive metals. Kept in the open, they react so vigorously with oxygen (and moisture) that they catch fire.
Kerosene does not react with them. It cuts off their contact with air and prevents accidental fires.
They are soft solids, not liquids. Kerosene also does not change them into oxides.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (alloy) with List-II (constituents).
List-I:
(A) Brass
(B) Bronze
(C) Solder
(D) Stainless steel
List-II:
(i) Lead and tin
(ii) Iron, nickel and chromium
(iii) Copper and tin
(iv) Copper and zinc
options: A-(iv), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(ii)
A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(ii)
A-(iv), B-(i), C-(iii), D-(ii)
A-(i), B-(iii), C-(iv), D-(ii)
questions.explanation:
(A) Brass is copper and zinc, so A-(iv).
(B) Bronze is copper and tin, so B-(iii).
(C) Solder is lead and tin, so C-(i).
(D) Stainless steel is iron, nickel and chromium, so D-(ii).
A common mistake is to swap brass and bronze, which gives option (2).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The hydrogen gas evolved when calcium reacts with cold water catches fire immediately.
Reason (R): Heat is evolved when calcium reacts with water.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is false. Calcium reacts less violently than sodium or potassium, and the heat released is not enough to ignite the hydrogen.
R is true. The reaction does release heat, only less than that of Na or K.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Element A has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 3 and element B has 2, 8, 6. They combine by electron transfer to form an ionic compound. How many electrons in total are transferred from A to B in forming one formula unit of the compound?
questions.explanation:
A (2, 8, 3) loses 3 electrons to form $A^{3+}$.
B (2, 8, 6) gains 2 electrons to form $B^{2-}$.
For the compound to be neutral, the total positive and negative charges must balance. The LCM of 3 and 2 is 6, so the formula is $A_2B_3$.
Two A atoms lose 3 electrons each, giving 6 electrons in total, which are accepted by three B atoms (2 each).
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Solid sodium chloride does not conduct electricity, but molten sodium chloride does.
Reason (R): Solid sodium chloride does not contain any ions; ions are formed only when it melts.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: ionic compounds do not conduct electricity as solids but do conduct when molten.
R is false: solid NaCl is made of ions. It is an aggregate of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions, not molecules.
In the solid, the rigid structure stops these ions from moving. Heating overcomes the attraction between the ions, so they move freely in the melt and carry current.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: Heating zinc carbonate strongly in limited air to convert it into zinc oxide is called calcination.
Statement II: When zinc blende (ZnS) is roasted, carbon dioxide gas is given off.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: carbonate ores are changed into oxides by strong heating in limited air. This is calcination: ZnCO$_3$ → ZnO + CO$_2$.
Statement II is incorrect: roasting ZnS in excess air gives sulphur dioxide, not CO$_2$: 2ZnS + 3O$_2$ → 2ZnO + 2SO$_2$.
CO$_2$ is the gas released during calcination of the carbonate.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: Zinc carbonate ore is converted into zinc oxide by heating it strongly in the presence of excess air, a process called roasting.
Statement II: Sulphide and carbonate ores of moderately reactive metals are first converted into oxides because it is easier to obtain a metal from its oxide.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Roasting means heating in excess air and is used for SULPHIDE ores, such as 2ZnS + 3O2 → 2ZnO + 2SO2.
A carbonate ore like ZnCO3 is heated strongly in LIMITED air. This is calcination: ZnCO3 → ZnO + CO2.
Statement II is correct: NCERT notes that a metal is more easily obtained from its oxide. The oxide is then reduced with carbon.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which of the following metal oxides reacts with both dilute hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide solution to form a salt and water?
options: Zinc oxide
Sodium oxide
Magnesium oxide
Copper(II) oxide
questions.explanation:
Oxides that react with both acids and bases to give salt and water are called amphoteric oxides. NCERT gives aluminium oxide and zinc oxide as examples.
$Na_2O$, $MgO$ and $CuO$ are basic oxides. They react with acids but not with bases.
So zinc oxide is the only amphoteric oxide among the options.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following ions have the same electronic configuration as neon?
$Na^+$, $Mg^{2+}$, $Cl^-$, $O^{2-}$, $K^+$, $F^-$, $Ca^{2+}$, $Al^{3+}$
questions.explanation:
Neon has 10 electrons, arranged as 2, 8.
The following ions each have 10 electrons: $Na^+$ (11 − 1), $Mg^{2+}$ (12 − 2), $O^{2-}$ (8 + 2), $F^-$ (9 + 1) and $Al^{3+}$ (13 − 3). That makes 5 ions.
$Cl^-$ (17 + 1), $K^+$ (19 − 1) and $Ca^{2+}$ (20 − 2) each have 18 electrons (2, 8, 8), which matches argon instead.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
A metal X has the following features:
(i) Its oxide reacts with HCl as well as with NaOH, forming salt and water in each case.
(ii) It reacts with steam but not with cold or hot water.
(iii) It is extracted by electrolytic reduction of its oxide, because carbon cannot reduce this oxide.
Identify X.
options: Zinc
Aluminium
Magnesium
Iron
questions.explanation:
Clue (i) points to an amphoteric oxide, which means $Al_2O_3$ or ZnO.
Clue (ii) fits Al, Zn and Fe. It rules out Mg, which reacts with hot water.
Clue (iii) is decisive. ZnO is reduced by carbon, but aluminium is obtained by electrolysis of $Al_2O_3$. Aluminium has more affinity for oxygen than carbon does.
Iron fails (i) and (iii), and magnesium oxide is basic, not amphoteric.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
A metal X shows three properties:
(1) It reacts with dilute HCl to give hydrogen, but the bubbles form slowly and the temperature rises only a little.
(2) X displaces copper from copper sulphate solution.
(3) Zinc displaces X from a solution of a salt of X.
The metal X is most likely:
options: Magnesium
Aluminium
Iron
Copper
questions.explanation:
From (2), X is more reactive than Cu. This rules out copper.
From (3), X is less reactive than Zn. This rules out Mg and Al, which are both above Zn.
From (1), the slow bubbling and small heat release fit the lowest metal in the order Mg > Al > Zn > Fe.
Iron satisfies all three conditions.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Sodium metal is stored under kerosene oil in the laboratory.
Reason (R): Sodium reacts so vigorously with oxygen that it can catch fire when kept in the open.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: sodium and potassium are kept immersed in kerosene oil.
R is true: these metals react so vigorously with oxygen that they catch fire if left in the open.
Kerosene keeps air (oxygen and moisture) away from the metal. This prevents accidental fires, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which allotrope of carbon is a conductor of electricity?
options: Diamond
Graphite
Coal tar
Charcoal ash
questions.explanation:
Carbon exists in different forms called allotropes.
Among them, NCERT identifies graphite as a conductor of electricity, an exception among non-metals.
Diamond, the other allotrope discussed, is known for its hardness and high melting point, not for conducting electricity.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Elements cannot be classified as metals or non-metals on the basis of their physical properties alone.
Reason (R): Several elements, such as mercury (a liquid metal) and iodine (a lustrous non-metal), show physical properties that do not fit their group.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT concludes that physical properties alone cannot group elements because there are many exceptions.
R is true: mercury is a metal that is liquid at room temperature, and iodine is a non-metal with lustre.
These exceptions are exactly why physical properties fail as a basis for classification, so R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A teacher says that two metals have such low melting points that they would melt if kept on your palm. Which pair is she referring to?
options: Sodium and potassium
Gallium and caesium
Mercury and lead
Aluminium and zinc
questions.explanation:
Most metals have high melting points, but NCERT names gallium and caesium as exceptions with very low melting points.
The warmth of the palm is enough to melt them.
Sodium and potassium are soft and have low melting points, but NCERT gives gallium and caesium as the examples that melt on the palm.
Mercury is already a liquid, and lead does not melt in the hand.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Bells used in schools are made of metals and not of wood or plastic. Which property of metals is mainly responsible for this?
options: Malleability
Sonority
Ductility
Metallic lustre
questions.explanation:
Metals that produce a ringing sound when they strike a hard surface are called sonorous.
A school bell must give a loud, clear sound when struck, so it is made of a sonorous metal.
Malleability lets a metal be beaten into sheets. It explains how the bell can be shaped, not why it rings.
Ductility and lustre have nothing to do with sound.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: During electrolytic refining of copper, the electrolyte used is:
options: Dilute hydrochloric acid
Molten sodium chloride
Acidified copper sulphate solution
Aqueous zinc sulphate solution
questions.explanation:
The electrolyte in electrolytic refining is a solution of a salt of the metal being refined.
For copper, NCERT uses a solution of acidified copper sulphate.
It supplies the copper ions that deposit on the cathode.
Molten NaCl is electrolysed to extract sodium, not to refine copper.
Zinc sulphate contains the wrong metal ions.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Compounds formed by the transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal are known as:
options: Covalent compounds
Amphoteric compounds
Electrovalent compounds
Alloys
questions.explanation:
When a metal loses electrons and a non-metal gains them, cations and anions are formed.
The compounds formed in this way are called ionic or electrovalent compounds. Examples are NaCl and $MgCl_2$.
Covalent compounds are formed by sharing of electrons, not by transfer.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (process) with List-II (name of the process):
List-I
(a) ZnS heated strongly in excess air
(b) ZnCO3 heated strongly in limited air
(c) Fe2O3 heated with aluminium powder to join railway tracks
(d) Electrolysis of molten NaCl to obtain sodium
List-II
(i) Electrolytic reduction
(ii) Calcination
(iii) Roasting
(iv) Thermit reaction
questions.explanation:
(a) Heating a sulphide ore in excess air converts it to an oxide. This is roasting, so (a)-(iii).
(b) Heating a carbonate ore in limited air converts it to an oxide. This is calcination, so (b)-(ii).
(c) Aluminium displaces iron from Fe2O3 and gives molten iron. This is the thermit reaction, so (c)-(iv).
(d) Sodium is too reactive to be reduced by carbon, so it is obtained by electrolytic reduction, giving (d)-(i).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (alloy) with List-II (constituents):
List-I: (P) Brass (Q) Bronze (R) Solder (S) Stainless steel
List-II: (i) Lead and tin (ii) Copper and tin (iii) Iron, nickel and chromium (iv) Copper and zinc
options: P-ii, Q-iv, R-i, S-iii
P-iv, Q-ii, R-i, S-iii
P-iv, Q-i, R-ii, S-iii
P-i, Q-ii, R-iv, S-iii
questions.explanation:
Brass is copper + zinc, so P matches (iv).
Bronze is copper + tin, so Q matches (ii).
Solder is lead + tin, so R matches (i).
Stainless steel is iron + nickel + chromium, so S matches (iii).
Students often swap brass and bronze. Remember that bronze contains tin.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
The melting points of some ionic compounds are given:
NaCl: 1074 K, LiCl: 887 K, CaCl$_2$: 1045 K, CaO: 2850 K, MgCl$_2$: 981 K
Which option arranges them in increasing order of melting point?
options: LiCl < MgCl$_2$ < CaCl$_2$ < NaCl < CaO
LiCl < CaCl$_2$ < MgCl$_2$ < NaCl < CaO
MgCl$_2$ < LiCl < NaCl < CaCl$_2$ < CaO
CaO < NaCl < CaCl$_2$ < MgCl$_2$ < LiCl
questions.explanation:
Arrange the compounds from the lowest value to the highest:
LiCl (887 K), then MgCl$_2$ (981 K), then CaCl$_2$ (1045 K), then NaCl (1074 K), then CaO (2850 K).
Option (2) swaps CaCl$_2$ and MgCl$_2$.
Option (4) gives the decreasing order, not the increasing order.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A sodium ion carries a net charge of +1.
Reason (R): After sodium loses its outermost electron, its nucleus still has 11 protons but only 10 electrons remain.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation:
A is true: $Na \rightarrow Na^+ + e^-$, so the ion carries a unit positive charge.
R is true: Na (2, 8, 1) loses its M-shell electron and becomes 2, 8. The number of protons stays at 11, while the number of electrons drops to 10.
The one excess proton is exactly why the ion has a +1 charge, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Three metals X, Y and Z were tested with salt solutions:
- X displaces zinc from zinc sulphate solution.
- Y displaces copper from copper sulphate solution but does not displace iron from iron(II) sulphate solution.
- Z does not displace copper from copper sulphate solution but displaces silver from silver nitrate solution.
Which option gives the correct decreasing order of reactivity and a possible identity of Y?
options: X > Z > Y; Y could be lead
X > Y > Z; Y could be lead
X > Y > Z; Y could be zinc
Z > Y > X; Y could be aluminium
questions.explanation:
X displaces Zn, so X is above zinc and is highly reactive.
Y lies above Cu but below Fe, so Y is between iron and copper.
Z lies below Cu but above Ag, so Z is the least reactive of the three.
This gives the order X > Y > Z.
In the activity series, lead sits between Fe and Cu, so Y could be lead.
Zinc would displace iron from FeSO4, so option (3) fails.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): During electrolytic refining of a metal, the mass of the cathode increases with time.
Reason (R): An amount of pure metal equivalent to that dissolving from the anode is deposited from the electrolyte onto the cathode.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: pure metal keeps depositing on the cathode strip, so its mass increases.
R is true: as metal dissolves from the anode, an equivalent amount of pure metal is deposited from the electrolyte on the cathode.
R directly explains why the cathode gains mass.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Ionic compounds such as sodium chloride have high melting and boiling points. Which of the following best explains this?
options: Their molecules are very large and heavy
A considerable amount of energy is needed to overcome the strong attraction between oppositely charged ions
Weak forces between neutral molecules must be broken
Free electrons hold the particles together tightly
questions.explanation:
Ionic compounds are made of positive and negative ions held together by strong electrostatic forces.
Melting or boiling them means breaking this strong inter-ionic attraction, which needs a lot of energy. That is why their melting and boiling points are high.
Option (1) is wrong because NaCl does not exist as molecules. It exists as aggregates of ions.
Option (4) describes metals, not ionic compounds.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A jeweller makes a 30 g necklace from 22 carat gold. In such gold, 22 parts of pure gold are alloyed with 2 parts of copper or silver. What is the mass of pure gold in the necklace?
questions.explanation:
Given: total mass = 30 g. 22 carat means 22 parts of gold in 24 parts of alloy.
Formula: mass of gold = total mass × $\frac{22}{24}$
Substituting: $30 \times \frac{22}{24} = 27.5$
So the mass of pure gold = 27.5 g.
Option (4), 2.5 g, is the mass of copper or silver, not of gold.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: About 2 km of wire can be drawn from 1 g of gold. What length of wire can be drawn from 3.5 g of gold, assuming the wire has the same thickness?
options: 7 km
3.5 km
14 km
questions.explanation:
Given: 1 g of gold gives 2 km of wire. Mass available = 3.5 g.
Formula: For the same thickness, length is proportional to mass, so length = 2 km per gram × mass.
Substituting: length = 2 × 3.5 = 7 km.
So the length of the wire = 7 km. This shows that gold is the most ductile metal.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which of the following non-metals is a liquid at room temperature?
options: Iodine
Sulphur
Bromine
Phosphorus
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that non-metals are either solids or gases, with bromine as the only exception because it is a liquid.
Iodine, sulphur and phosphorus are all solids at room temperature.
Iodine is tempting because it is an exception in another way (it is lustrous), but it is still a solid.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: Iodine is a non-metal, yet it has a lustrous appearance.
Statement II: Graphite is a form of a non-metal that conducts electricity.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: NCERT lists iodine as a lustrous non-metal, an exception to the usual properties.
Statement II is correct: graphite is an allotrope of carbon, a non-metal, and it conducts electricity.
Both are exceptions that show elements cannot be classified by physical properties alone.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
A student lists some observations about elements that do not fit the general physical properties of metals and non-metals. How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Bromine is a non-metal that exists as a liquid at room temperature.
(ii) Diamond, an allotrope of carbon, is a good conductor of electricity.
(iii) Gallium and caesium are metals with melting points so low that they melt when kept on the palm.
(iv) Lithium, sodium and potassium are hard metals with high densities.
(v) Iodine is a non-metal but has a lustrous surface.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: non-metals are solids or gases, and bromine is the only liquid exception.
(ii) Incorrect: graphite is the allotrope of carbon that conducts electricity. Diamond is the hardest natural substance and has a very high melting point.
(iii) Correct: gallium and caesium are metals with very low melting points.
(iv) Incorrect: alkali metals are so soft that they can be cut with a knife, and they have low densities.
(v) Correct: iodine is lustrous even though it is a non-metal.
So 3 statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (metal) with List-II (behaviour with water):
List-I: (a) Potassium (b) Magnesium (c) Zinc (d) Silver
List-II: (i) Reacts only with steam (ii) No reaction at all (iii) Reacts violently with cold water; hydrogen catches fire (iv) Reacts with hot water and floats
questions.explanation:
(a) Potassium reacts violently and exothermically with cold water, so the hydrogen catches fire: (iii).
(b) Magnesium reacts with hot water and floats due to hydrogen bubbles: (iv).
(c) Zinc reacts only with steam: (i).
(d) Silver does not react with water: (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Sodium metal in a school laboratory is always stored under kerosene oil. What is the main reason for this practice?
options: Sodium dissolves in kerosene and forms a stable solution
Sodium reacts so vigorously with oxygen that it can catch fire in the open, and kerosene keeps air and moisture away from it
Kerosene reacts with sodium to form a protective oxide layer on its surface
Sodium is a liquid at room temperature and needs to be kept in a container with oil
questions.explanation:
Key fact: NCERT states that potassium and sodium react so vigorously with oxygen that they catch fire if kept in the open.
Kerosene does not react with sodium. It simply cuts off contact with air and moisture, which prevents accidental fires.
Option (3) is the most tempting wrong choice, but kerosene does not create any oxide layer. Option (4) fails because sodium is a solid; mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: In an experiment on rusting, an iron nail is kept in a test tube with boiled distilled water, and about 1 mL of oil is poured on top before corking. What is the purpose of boiling the water and adding the oil layer?
options: To remove moisture so that the nail stays completely dry
To remove dissolved air from the water and stop fresh air from dissolving in it
To kill bacteria that would otherwise speed up rusting
To coat the nail with oil so that water cannot touch it
questions.explanation:
Boiling the water drives out the air dissolved in it.
The oil floats on the water and prevents air from dissolving again.
The nail is therefore exposed to water but not to air, and it does not rust.
Option (1) is wrong because the nail is still in water. Drying the air is the job of anhydrous CaCl$_2$ in a different tube.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (sample of sodium chloride) with List-II (behaviour in an electric circuit).
List-I:
(P) Dry solid crystal
(Q) Dissolved in water
(R) Shaken with kerosene
(S) Strongly heated until molten
List-II:
(1) No conduction; the salt does not dissolve, so no free ions are available
(2) No conduction; ions are held in a rigid structure
(3) Conducts; heat overcomes the electrostatic attraction so ions move freely
(4) Conducts; ions in solution move to the opposite electrodes
questions.explanation:
P: In the solid, the ions are fixed in a rigid structure, so there is no conduction. This matches (2).
Q: In water, the salt dissolves and the mobile ions move to the electrodes. This matches (4).
R: NaCl is insoluble in kerosene, so there are no free ions in the liquid. This matches (1).
S: In the melt, heat overcomes the inter-ionic attraction and the ions move freely. This matches (3).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes an ore from a mineral?
options: Every ore is a mineral, but only those minerals from which a metal can be profitably extracted are ores
Every mineral is an ore, but only ores occur naturally in the earth's crust
Ores are found only in seawater, while minerals are found in the earth's crust
Minerals contain metals in the free state, while ores contain only compounds
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: minerals are elements or compounds that occur naturally in the earth's crust.
Ores are minerals that contain a very high percentage of a particular metal, so the metal can be extracted from them profitably.
So every ore is a mineral, but not every mineral is an ore. This makes (1) correct.
Option (2) reverses the relationship.
Options (3) and (4) are not supported by the text.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which one of the following metals is found in the free (native) state in the earth's crust?
options: Magnesium
Calcium
Gold
Zinc
questions.explanation:
Metals at the bottom of the activity series are the least reactive, so they can be found in the free state. NCERT gives gold, silver, platinum and copper as examples.
Magnesium and calcium are near the top of the series. They are so reactive that they are never found free in nature.
Zinc is moderately reactive. It occurs mainly as oxide, sulphide or carbonate ores.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A clean iron nail is dipped in copper sulphate solution and left for about 20 minutes. Which observation is expected?
options: The nail stays unchanged and the solution stays blue
A reddish-brown coating forms on the nail and the blue solution fades to pale green
A silvery coating forms on the nail and the solution turns colourless
Gas bubbles form on the nail and the solution turns deep blue
questions.explanation:
Iron is above copper in the activity series, so it displaces copper from copper sulphate solution.
Fe + CuSO4 → FeSO4 + Cu
The copper set free deposits on the nail as a reddish-brown coat.
Blue CuSO4 is replaced by pale green FeSO4, so the colour changes.
No gas is produced in this reaction, so option (4) is wrong.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Food cans are coated with tin rather than zinc because zinc is more reactive than tin.
(ii) Pure iron is preferred for construction because it is hard and does not stretch when hot.
(iii) Silver articles turn black in air due to a coating of silver oxide.
(iv) The iron pillar near the Qutub Minar was built over 1600 years ago and has resisted rusting.
(v) Mixing iron with nickel and chromium gives stainless steel, which is hard and does not rust.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: zinc is more reactive than tin and could react with food, so tin is used.
(ii) Incorrect: pure iron is very soft and stretches easily when hot. It becomes hard with about 0.05% carbon.
(iii) Incorrect: silver reacts with sulphur in air to form black silver sulphide, not silver oxide.
(iv) Correct, as stated in NCERT.
(v) Correct.
So 3 statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 · Metals and Non-metals

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (experiment) with List-II (observation).
List-I:
A. Iron nail in copper sulphate solution
B. Copper wire in silver nitrate solution
C. Copper wire in iron(II) sulphate solution
D. Zinc granules in dilute hydrochloric acid
List-II:
(i) No visible change
(ii) Blue solution turns pale green; brown deposit on the metal
(iii) Colourless solution slowly turns blue; shiny greyish-white deposit on the metal
(iv) Gas bubbles that burn with a pop sound
options: A-(iii), B-(ii), C-(i), D-(iv)
A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(iv)
A-(ii), B-(i), C-(iii), D-(iv)
A-(iv), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(ii)
questions.explanation:
A: Fe displaces Cu. Green FeSO4 forms and brown Cu deposits, so A-(ii).
B: Cu displaces Ag. Blue copper nitrate forms and silver deposits, so B-(iii).
C: Cu is less reactive than Fe, so there is no reaction. C-(i).
D: Zn is above H and releases H2, which burns with a pop. D-(iv).
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Elements cannot be classified as metals or non-metals on the basis of physical properties alone, because there are exceptions. Which of the following statements correctly describes such an exception?
options: Mercury is a non-metal that is a liquid at room temperature
Diamond is a form of carbon that is a good conductor of electricity
Iodine is a non-metal, yet it has a lustrous surface
Sodium is a metal that is too hard to be cut with a knife
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect: mercury is a metal. The non-metal that is a liquid is bromine.
(2) Incorrect: graphite is the allotrope of carbon that conducts electricity. Diamond is the hardest natural substance.
(3) Correct: iodine is a non-metal but it shows lustre.
(4) Incorrect: alkali metals such as sodium are so soft that they can be cut with a knife.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Consider the reaction:
$3MnO_2(s) + 4Al(s) \rightarrow 3Mn(l) + 2Al_2O_3(s) + Heat$
How many of the following statements about it are correct?
(i) Aluminium is oxidised.
(ii) Manganese dioxide is reduced.
(iii) The reaction absorbs heat from the surroundings.
(iv) Manganese is produced in the molten state.
(v) Aluminium can act as the reducing agent because it is more reactive than manganese.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: Al gains oxygen and becomes Al$_2$O$_3$.
(ii) Correct: MnO$_2$ loses oxygen and becomes Mn.
(iii) Incorrect: such displacement reactions are highly exothermic, so heat is released, not absorbed.
(iv) Correct: the heat released is large enough that Mn is formed as a liquid, Mn(l).
(v) Correct: a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one from its compound.
So 4 statements are correct.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A chlorine atom (atomic number 17) gains one electron when it reacts with sodium. What is the electronic configuration (K, L, M) of the chloride ion formed?
questions.explanation:
Chlorine has 17 electrons, arranged as 2, 8, 7.
It has 7 valence electrons and needs one more to complete its octet.
On gaining one electron, it has 18 electrons, arranged as 2, 8, 8. This is the argon configuration.
Option (1), 2, 8, 7, is the neutral atom. Option (3), 2, 8, 6, would mean losing an electron.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Consider the metals: aluminium, iron, zinc, magnesium, copper, lead, calcium.
How many of these react with steam but react neither with cold water nor with hot water?
questions.explanation:
Aluminium, iron and zinc: no reaction with cold or hot water, but they react with steam. These are the three that count.
Magnesium: reacts with hot water, so it does not count.
Calcium: reacts with cold water, so it does not count.
Copper and lead: do not react with water at all.
Answer: (2)

questions.question: Which of the following metals does not react with cold water but reacts with hot water to form its hydroxide and hydrogen gas?
options: Sodium
Magnesium
Iron
Copper
questions.explanation:
Magnesium does not react with cold water. With hot water it forms magnesium hydroxide and hydrogen.
Sodium is wrong because it reacts violently even with cold water.
Iron reacts only with steam.
Copper does not react with water at all.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Zinc does not evolve hydrogen gas when it reacts with nitric acid.
Reason (R): Nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent that oxidises the hydrogen produced to water and is itself reduced to nitrogen oxides.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Metals generally do not give hydrogen gas with nitric acid. Only magnesium and manganese do so, and only with very dilute HNO3.
R is true. HNO3 oxidises the H2 to water and is itself reduced to N2O, NO or NO2.
The oxidation of hydrogen is exactly why no H2 is released, so R explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Non-metals are generally poor conductors of electricity. Which of the following non-metals is an exception and conducts electricity?
options: Iodine
Graphite
Sulphur
Diamond
questions.explanation:
Non-metals are usually bad conductors of heat and electricity. NCERT names graphite as the exception.
Graphite is an allotrope of carbon, and it conducts electricity.
Iodine is tempting because it is also an exception, but for lustre, not for conduction.
Diamond is another allotrope of carbon. It is known for its hardness, not for conducting electricity.
Answer: (2)
